source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 5 database (period comparison), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Each period of a comparison gives its start, its end and its number of days; amounts are never scaled to the period's length.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 5 database (period comparison), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A category is one line across periods by its identity, under its current name and in its current place, also when it was renamed, ended, restored, emptied into "Other" or left void by a reopen; where it was not in force it plans nothing (empty, not zero) but still counts what was spent on it; in two periods side by side, a period where the category has nothing at all is empty, not zero.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 5 database (period comparison), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The comparison reads catch the budget up like opening it does and write nothing else; while a very long absence is still being caught up they answer that it is (catching_up) instead of a shortened range.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 5 database (period comparison), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Only members of a budget can read its comparison; another user and an anonymous visitor get nothing.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 5 database (period comparison), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: No read returns more rows than the API delivers in one response (1000) without paging: a list that can grow beyond it is read a page at a time (periods, transactions, a debt's history); the kinds read one row each (categories, subscriptions, debts) are bounded at 900 rows per budget, void ones included; the spending per category returns one row per category line; and the reopen preview lists at most 1000 rows, the last one counting the rest.
source: owner-request: coordinator finding on the step 5 database (API row limit), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: No call of any kind creates more than one bounded step of periods, however often it calls the catch-up: ensure_periods and get_current_period do one step and keep it; every other read, preview and write does at most its own roll-over (R-PERIOD-250) and, when the budget is still behind, answers catching_up and changes nothing.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent re-review of the step 4 database fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: While a charge of a subscription is due and held back by the transaction limit, its schedule (cadence or next charge date, from now or as a correction) cannot change and it cannot end (charge_held_back, in the previews too); its name, price and category can; its next charge date shows the held date, and so does the first date of its schedule preview.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent re-review of the step 4 database fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A period's interest for a debt is computed once, when the period is created, on the balance from everything dated before the period's start (opening, payments, adjustments, earlier interest), whatever day the catch-up runs; a debt not opened before the period's start gets none for it; a period created again after a reopen gets it again by the same rule.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent re-review of the step 4 database fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A debt's history can also be read newest first, a page at a time with the same cursor, each row with the same running balance as oldest first.
The transactions list says, per transaction, whether it is a payment of a debt that has ended (and so cannot be changed, unlinked or deleted).

An imported expense or refund without a category from the member or a rule goes to the budget's "to categorise" category, created at the first import that needs it; every transaction keeps a category, so every total and comparison still adds up.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A merchant rule matches a row when the row's merchant key (from its merchant, else its description: lower case, accents and punctuation removed, the statement's words and a processor prefix dropped) contains the rule's fragment; the longest fragment wins, and a rule applies only where its category is in force.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Creating a rule in one click can move, in the same call, the other transactions to review waiting in "to categorise" whose key contains it; the answer says how many moved; transactions already in a real category stay.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A row is a possible match of an existing transaction of the same kind that was not imported, with the same amount and a date within three days either way; it is skipped by default, and when the match is a charge awaiting confirmation the import confirms it; each existing transaction absorbs one row of a batch.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Skipped rows of a batch can be imported anyway, one by one or all at once, through the same import.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: An import token imports only with the default choices and never confirms a charge; it reads nothing back beyond counts and the reasons of rows refused for their own content; an unknown, expired or revoked token, or one whose creator is no longer a member, gets one refusal before any lock or catch-up; its calls and rows are limited over rolling windows of 60 minutes and 24 hours.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A member can undo an import batch once: its transactions still to review are deleted, the confirmed ones and the charges it confirmed stay, and it takes no more rows.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A category's first subcategory moves its merchant rules to "Other"; a category deleted takes its rules with it; an ended category's rules stay and apply where it is in force.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: An import is sent as a batch of up to 100 chunks of up to 500 rows (250 by a token) under an id the caller generates; a chunk sent again records nothing and answers as the first time; a chunk the transaction limit cannot hold is refused whole, saying how many rows would fit.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A transaction to review is confirmed one by one or all at once, never while it is in "to categorise"; the budget says how many are to review and the transactions list can show only them or one batch.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The "to categorise" category takes no subcategory and no expectation, can be renamed, and cannot end while it holds transactions.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A visitor without a session can call only the token import; every other import function and every import table refuses them.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A budget has at most 50 accounts and 50 planned transfers in force, and 200 of each in all (void ones not counted); each overview stays within 900 rows.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The accounts named by a planned transfer's or an income's terms, and the category of a transfer's terms (a leaf), are in force in every period those terms govern.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Closing an account that the terms of a transfer or an income still use from then on is refused, naming what uses it; an account never named and never counted before is deleted instead; earlier periods keep a closed account.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The previews of creating and editing a planned transfer give, with the write's own code, the due dates and amounts of the periods its terms govern (the next periods at their projected boundaries) and the transactions the write creates at once; the preview of ending one gives its outcome and what it removes.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Ending a planned transfer removes its occurrences from that period on; every mark already made and every transaction link stay, and the period's checklist still lists the transfer, flagged as ended; a transfer that never counted before and was never marked is deleted instead.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database, step 7 change, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The money flow of a period adds up: its incomes total the period's salaries, each income flows into its account or into "not assigned", and each account shows what comes in, what goes out and what stays (negative when more is planned out than comes in), never a balance.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: An income can name the account it is paid into, as part of its terms, versioned with them.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A reopen moves a mark of the merged period to the reopened period when that period has none for the transfer; otherwise the mark goes, the catch-up's transaction with it, a member's transaction staying as an ordinary transaction; preview_reopen lists each.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16
rules.retiredBecause: D-430 replaced moving and removing the merged period's marks with marks keyed by date that a reopen never moves (R-ACCOUNT-306).

rules.statement: A planned transfer linked to a category commits its planned amount in that category in each period it is in force, shown apart from the subscriptions' committed amount.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A planned transfer has exactly one occurrence in each period it is in force. Its due date is the first date with the chosen day on or after the period's start (clamped to the month's length, no weekend rule), or the chosen income's actual pay date in the period plus an offset of 0 to 31 days (the period's start for the primary income, and where the chosen income is not in force); never after the period's last day.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16
rules.retiredBecause: D-420 replaced "exactly one occurrence per period, capped at its last day" with occurrences on the calendar or per pay date (R-ACCOUNT-300, R-ACCOUNT-301).

rules.statement: Deleting the transaction of a done transfer puts it back: a manual one is to do again; an automatic one is not done and its transaction is not created again. Undoing a mark restores what the occurrence is without one: to do, or assumed done with its transaction.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The dashboard counts the manual transfers of the current period and of the period before it still to do, and those of them whose due date has passed.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A category that the terms of a planned transfer use from a period on cannot end from then (category_in_use names the transfer), and its first subcategory moves the transfer's category to "Other".
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A mark of a transfer's occurrence names the revision of the mark the member read (0: none); a mark made or changed since is refused with record_changed.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 database (accounts and money flow), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: What is stored of a row that was not imported is bounded: its known keys within their limits, and only the names of unknown keys; a call whose rows exceed 2 MB is refused whole when the function starts; the request body itself is read and parsed before the function runs, bounded only by the gateway (Q-280).
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Each existing transaction absorbs at most one row of a batch, as its duplicate or its match, counted over the whole batch whatever chunks it is sent in, in whatever order, and however often a chunk is sent again.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A preview names the batch its rows will be sent in; a preview with no batch id says what the first chunk of a new batch does, exactly as the write.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A transaction's review state changes only through confirming it (one or all); an edit, a link or an unlink leaves a transaction to review to review.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: An imported transaction keeps the amount, date and description it was first imported with; a statement line equal to those is a duplicate even after the member edited the transaction.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The merchant key handles a reference after the merchant, the statement's leading words, a processor prefix, any script, and letters such as ß and œ; the key of a key is itself.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A budget holds at most 10 import tokens that can still be used; a revoked or expired token can be deleted, and those kept are pruned to the newest 20 and to 365 days.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Import batches, skipped rows and remembered choices are read through paged functions only; a budget keeps at most 1000 remembered choices, the least recently used going first.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A batch's counts add up to the rows it received, also after rows are imported anyway; a row imported anyway answers with its original chunk and row number, and can be imported anyway again once its transaction is deleted.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A credit of exactly an income's amount is a salary when it is dated within five days either side of a period start: on or after the start of its own period, or before the start of the next period (projected when that period does not exist yet), at the income's amount in force in that period.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Neither undoing a batch nor applying a merchant rule changes a transaction linked to a subscription, a debt or a planned transfer, or a frozen one; undo says how many it kept and why.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A possible match goes to the row nearest in date (either way, within three days, same kind and amount); ties go to the earlier row, then to a charge awaiting confirmation.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every refusal of the import is a stable code: a decimal amount is invalid_amount for its row, two budgets racing for one batch id get import_batch_conflict, a bad name for "to categorise" is invalid_name.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A statement the reader refuses is explained in words for every reason it gives (with the control, both figures, the language or the limit where it has one); the line in question is shown on the device only, apart from the explanation, and is never logged, stored or sent; nothing is sent to the budget.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The preview is asked under the batch id the import will use, with exactly the rows it will send; a changed choice is asked again (debounced), the rows whose answer is on its way are marked as being checked and never shown as current, and the import is offered only once every part has a current answer; the summary counts the rows the database answered, and no amount is added up in the client.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The import sends its parts in order under one batch id; a part whose answer is lost is sent again with the same number and the same rows; a budget that must catch up first is caught up and the part sent again; the transaction limit stops the import and says how many rows would fit and that nothing of that part was written.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: While an import is sent, leaving the page asks first; an interrupted import is noted on the device (its batch id and a fingerprint of its rows, never the rows) and the page says so; the same statement opened again goes on under the same batch, so what was recorded is not recorded twice.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The CSV import reads quoted cells (separators, doubled quotes and line breaks inside), a byte-order mark and CRLF, a UTF-16 file with or without its byte-order mark, UTF-8 and Windows-1252, and refuses with the reason a file that is not text or cannot be decoded; removes a control character (a NUL…) from a cell on the device and names its line; detects the separator among comma, semicolon and tab and lets the user change it; asks for the date format whenever the dates can be read more than one way; reads the decimal mark from the amounts of the whole file and asks for it when they do not settle it (one mark followed by exactly three digits, as in 1.200, is ambiguous), saying it could not be decided, never assuming one, and refuses a file whose lines contradict each other, naming them; reads amounts into integer rappen without floating-point arithmetic, with a stated sign or two columns; lists every line it cannot read with its line number and why, and sends none of them; remembers the mapping per budget on the device only.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Text from a bank file or a token (descriptions, merchants, details, token and category names) is rendered as text only, never as markup or a link, isolated so that right-to-left characters cannot reorder the words around it, and wraps rather than widening the page.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A new import token's secret is shown once, with a copy button and where to put it (the environment of the session that runs the script, never a conversation); it is held only in that dialog while it is open: never in the address, browser storage, the query or mutation cache, or a log.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every name and description goes through one cleaner: control, bidirectional and zero-width characters are removed (a joiner between two visible characters stays, R-SECURITY-341), other white space becomes one space, and the result is trimmed; markup and formulas stay text (the screens escape, an export neutralises).
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A token's answer never depends on the budget's content beyond coarse states (room for fewer than 250 transactions, D-451; far behind; the import storage of the day used up, D-452; its budget's lock held for more than a second, D-453): every argument is checked before anything of the budget, and a token cannot name the "to categorise" category.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every call with a valid token that does work counts toward its limits, whatever its outcome (cancelled included); a busy answer (token_busy, imports_busy) does no work and does not count; the check and the count are one step under the token's own lock, over windows of whole minutes (R-SECURITY-342).
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A token stops when its creator leaves the budget, is removed from it, or deletes their account.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A token import records the token, never the caller, and cannot be called by GET (read-only calls are refused before the token is looked at).
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Only an imported transaction still to review can be in "to categorise": no hand-typed transaction, subscription, debt, planned transfer or merchant rule uses it; it does not count toward the 200 categories in force; my_budgets names it only while it is in force.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 6 database (import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: "To categorise" is marked in words wherever categories are listed (the budget page, progress, compare); it is offered as a target in no transaction, subscription, debt or rule form (an import waiting in it is edited to a real category); its form changes only the name, and its removal is not offered while it holds transactions, saying why.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A budget whose last period ended more than 62 days before today (or its end date), or that has room for transactions and a subscription charge or a transfer's transaction due that long ago not made yet, is caught up only by ensure_periods and get_current_period: every other call answers catching_up at once, before taking the budget lock and without doing any work; ensure_periods and get_current_period wait at most two seconds for a lock another session holds, then answer catching_up, never the statement timeout.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 5 database and the step 4 re-review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A user belongs to at most 50 budgets (owned ones included): accepting an invitation or creating a budget beyond that is refused (membership_limit_reached); the invitations shown to an invitee come a page at a time.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 5 database and the step 4 re-review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A call that creates a record (a transaction, an income, a category, a subscription, a debt, an account, a planned transfer) accepts a client-generated request id: sent again by the same member for the same budget, call and arguments, it creates nothing and answers what the first call created; any other use of a known id is refused (request_reused) and reveals nothing.
source: owner-request: coordinator, screen review of steps 4 and 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Whatever read or write answers catching_up (a tab left open across a long absence), the app catches the budget up (ensure_periods until it answers 0) behind the catching-up screen, then reads every query of the budget again; the page stays mounted underneath, so a refused save keeps what was typed and says that nothing was saved and that it can be saved again now. A catch-up that ends within a moment shows nothing different.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Periods are read a page at a time with list_periods (120, newest first); the periods page shows the newest and offers the older ones on request, saying how many are listed.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every period picker (the transactions filter, a correction's or a removal's period, a new record's first period, the progress view's step back) reaches the oldest period: while older periods exist than those read, its last entry "Older periods…" reads the next page.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A reopen preview that lists at most 1000 changes says how many more there are, in words, from its 'more' row.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A subscription whose next charge date has come is shown as waiting since that date, with the reason in words (the budget holds the most transactions it can); charge_held_back, from a schedule change, an end or the end dialog's preview, is said in words with what to do first.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: An ended debt cannot be edited: its menu says why, its form (if open) offers no save with the reason, and update_debt's debt_ended reads the same.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A debt's history table shows the latest events first, 50 at a time, older ones read with get_debt_history's newest-first cursor; the chart reads oldest first.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: "Keep mine" keeps exactly the fields (or D-160 groups) the user changed in this form, measured against what the form showed when they changed them, and takes every other field from what the database says now for what is being edited: the record's current values for an edit from now; for a correction, the chosen period's terms read again (a change another member made from now never enters the correction). "Load their version" uses the same "now". Every form field belongs to a view or is a declared control (the correction switch, its period, whose income it is): a field in neither fails the form's tests. Changing a correction's period keeps the values the user typed in fields they changed.
source: owner-request: coordinator, final review of the step 4 screens (addendum C), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A save whose answer is lost (network) is never reported as someone else's change: when the record read again holds what the form sent, the form says it was saved; when it does not, it says the connection failed and nothing was saved, and what was typed stays.
source: owner-request: coordinator, final review of the step 4 screens (addendum C), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: After a charge is answered (it went through, or it did not after its confirmation), from the dashboard card or the transactions filtered to those awaiting, the focus goes to the charge now in its place, else to a named place (the page's heading, the period filter), never to the page's body; the filtered list offers both answers on each row; removing a link filter moves the focus to the next filter or the period filter.
source: owner-request: coordinator, final review of the step 4 screens (addendum C), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: When the schedule preview of a subscription edit is refused because a charge is held back (charge_held_back, D-388), the form says so before saving and does not offer the save.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part A, contract changes), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The comparison is its own page, "Compare", in the sidebar right after the dashboard, with three views: the trend, the categories over time and two periods side by side. The view and its choices (6, 12 or 24 periods, the selected period, the lines drawn, the planned amounts shown, periods A and B, the order) are in the address, so a link opens the same view; the page loads with its charts only when opened.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The trend shows, for each period of the range, its dates, its number of days, its income, spending, planned total and result as get_period_trend gives them, in two charts (income and spending as columns with the planned total as a line; the result as columns from zero) and in a table listing every figure. The running period is marked in words and said never to be averaged; the averages say over how many completed periods they are taken, or "no completed period yet" instead of an amount; when period lengths differ by more than a tenth the page says amounts are not adjusted for length. Selecting a period offers to open it and to compare it with another.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The categories view lists every category line by period as get_category_trend gives it: groups at the top level, opened on their subcategories (the open ones kept in the address); each period column with its dates, its number of days and the year where it changes; each line's average after the periods; in each period the spending (a link to that category's transactions in that period, also when they net to zero), the planned amount on request, spending above the plan marked with a sign and words, and "—", said as not planned, where the category was not in force and nothing was recorded (never 0). When period lengths differ by more than a tenth it says amounts are not adjusted. A chart draws up to five lines the user picks (every tick counts, however quick), by default the three top-level lines with the highest average; each line has the hue, the mark and the dash of its slot, kept while others are added or removed, and the running period is shaded and named. On a phone the name column is narrow and wraps, so at 320 px at least one whole period column is readable beside it, and a focused cell is never hidden under the sticky column or header.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The categories view shows its lines only against the periods they belong to: get_category_trend's period_ids must equal get_period_trend's periods for the same count; when they differ (a period was created or merged between the two reads) both are read again, three times in all, and then the view reports an error with a retry rather than misaligned figures.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Side by side, the database chooses the default periods (no id sent); the user picks A and B among every period (older ones on request, a chosen old one still shown in its picker) and can swap them. The totals (income, spent, result, planned, subscriptions) then each category, in the budget's order or biggest changes first, show A, B and the difference B minus A with its sign, an arrow and its direction in words (never colour alone); on request each category's planned amount in A and B and its difference; a side with nothing is "—", said in words; each period's length is shown. On a phone each row stacks so the difference is read without scrolling sideways, nine-figure amounts included.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The compare page says so when a comparison needs a second period, when the budget has no categories yet, and when the budget has ended (the range ends at its last period); a read that fails says so with a retry; a read answered catching_up is handled like any other (R-PERIOD-190).
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens adapted to the database re-review and step 5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: An edit form says its change was saved only after a save whose answer was lost on the way (a failed connection), and only when the record now holds every value the form sent; a save the database refused (record_changed) is never reported as saved, even when another member saved the same value in one of its fields: the form keeps what was typed and offers the choice between their version and keeping one's own.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: When the answer to an add (a new transaction, category, income, subscription or debt) is lost on the way, the form says it may have been saved and to check the list before saving again, never that nothing was saved.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16
rules.retiredBecause: D-440: every add form sends one request id (p_client_id, D-390), so saving again after a lost answer records once; R-CONCURRENCY-320 says what the form says now.

rules.statement: When the answer to an add (a new transaction, category, income, subscription or debt) is lost on the way, the form keeps what was entered and says that saving again is safe; the retry carries the same request id and is recorded once. A request id the database calls reused gets a new one, and the form says plainly that the values had already been saved with other content and to check the list.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part A, contract changes), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The app takes a budget for ended only from the budget's own end: it has an end date, it is caught up, and the database then gives no current period. A missing current period alone (a catch-up under way) never makes a page say the budget has ended, and never turns an edit into a correction: an open form keeps its state.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A save that has nothing to send (every field as recorded) keeps the window open and says so; it never closes with a success message.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: No call waits without end: a call unanswered after 30 seconds fails like a lost connection (a read shows an error with a retry, a write says what a lost answer means for it).
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every count in a message is grouped like amounts (12'345), in both languages, by the one helper that formats counts; the plural is chosen from the number.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A read answered catching_up is not a failure: it is not retried meanwhile and never shows an error card; the page waits (a placeholder) while the budget is caught up, then reads again.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A period named in the address (a filter, a comparison side) keeps its meaning beyond the pages of periods loaded: it is read by its id and shown in its picker; an id that is not a uuid is never sent.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The confirmations that move a period's start ("this period's salary actually arrived on …" and "back to the schedule") say, as preview_move_period_start answers for that start, how many debts lose the interest added at the period's start (D-386).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part A, contract changes), 2026-11-16
rules.retiredBecause: D-467: a start on or before the opening of a debt with interest in the period is refused (R-DEBT-340), so no interest is removed and preview_move_period_start.interest_removed is always 0; the confirmations no longer present it.

rules.statement: The dates a transaction may take start at the budget's first period, read by itself, whatever pages of periods are loaded.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Wherever periods are labelled by day and month (chart axes, column headers), the year is written on the first one and wherever it changes, visibly, so no label stands for two years.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A difference is written with its sign before the currency in both directions ("+CHF 192.92", "−CHF 192.92"), everywhere a difference is shown; other negative amounts keep the money formatter's form.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A comparison chart takes the width while its periods fit (24 periods from 1024 px); when they do not, it scrolls inside its own frame: the value axis (with its unit, CHF) stays in view outside the frame, the frame shows whole periods only and opens on the newest, says that earlier periods are to the left, and can be focused (named) and scrolled with the keyboard.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A period in the address that is not one of the current budget's (another budget's, deleted, or not an id at all) is never sent as such: the comparison falls back to the default periods, says so in words and offers the pickers; choosing another budget drops the choices that named the previous budget's periods and lines.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: "Compare with…" on a period of the trend puts that period as B and the one before it as A (the first period has none: A is left to pick), so a period is never compared with itself.
source: owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A call with a client request id checks membership before the id, the catch-up gate and the budget lock: a signed-in outsider or a removed member gets budget_not_found for every budget and client id; a replay answers a current member only rows of the budget it names, and nothing for a record removed since.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A token call never waits for another token call: the same token busy answers token_busy, every slot for token work taken answers imports_busy, both at once, doing no work and counting nothing; a working call takes at most 250 rows, waits at most a second for its budget (budget_busy), and counts even when cancelled (call_cancelled).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The cleaner keeps a zero-width joiner or non-joiner between two characters that are not white space and removes it elsewhere; it removes interlinear annotation marks and the language tag; a text with nothing visible left is empty.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A token call counts toward the hour for at least 60 and at most 61 minutes and toward the day for at least 24 hours and at most 24 hours and 1 minute.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A token adds chunks only to a batch it created; any other existing batch id answers import_batch_conflict, a chunk already recorded included.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The token call checks its batch id, chunk and statement dates itself: a malformed one answers invalid_batch, invalid_chunk or invalid_date, never a raw cast error.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A token call is refused with transaction_limit_reached whenever the budget has room for fewer than 250 transactions, whatever rows it sends; a member is told how many rows would fit.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A statement previewed part by part with preview_import_part answers, for each part, the rows and counts the write of the same parts in the same order then gives (absent changes by others), with the totals of each part and of the statement so far: rows by action, and the rows to import by kind, count and amount.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A budget's import storage is bounded: in a rolling 24 hours at most 20 000 rows submitted, 50 new batches (import_limit_reached) and 20 tokens created, deleted ones included (token_limit_reached); kept at most 2 000 batches (empty ones go first), the newest 20 000 skipped rows and the newest 50 chunk answers of at most 7 days (an older chunk sent again answers chunk_expired).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

The question says how many rows, of which kinds (salary already planned, card bill payment, own transfer, transfer to a person, charge confirmed, entered by hand, duplicate, skipped by the member), and that they count twice if they are what the import thought; it sends exactly the rows it counted.

rules.statement: A planned transfer on a fixed day follows a calendar schedule like a subscription: a cadence (monthly, quarterly or yearly), a first date and its day of the month, clamped to the month's length, with no weekend rule; each date is an occurrence of the period that contains it, due that day, so a period may have none or several.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every occurrence is identified by its date: a pay-date transfer has one occurrence per pay date of its income in the period, keyed by the scheduled pay date and due on the actual pay date plus the offset, never after the end of the period containing it; marks are kept by that date, a call names the occurrence when its period has several, a member's mark whose occurrence is no longer planned stays listed in the period of its date, flagged, and one undo leads out of every mark.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Each period carries the scheduled pay date of the salary that started it; after any change of the plan the catch-up keeps exactly one transaction for each automatic occurrence linked to a category that is due (unless a member marked it or the budget is full) and none of its own for anything else, so a reopen followed by recording the salary again leaves one transaction for that payday.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every preview of a change the catch-up follows (creating, editing, correcting or ending a transfer, a reopen) says, with counts, which transactions of the catch-up it removes and creates and which members' marks lose or regain their occurrence, computed by the write itself (for an amount alone, which changes none of them, without running it).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The committed figures and the money flow count a transfer's monthly share (a quarterly or yearly amount divided by its months, half up), and the reads carry the real amount and cadence beside it.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: What was recorded stays: an occurrence keeps its mark and transaction when the transfer is later made manual or automatic, corrected or ended, a transaction already made keeps its amount and category when the terms are edited later, and a done date lies on or after the transfer's first counted day.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A reopen moves no mark: the catch-up's transaction of the merged period's payday goes until that salary is recorded again, a member's mark there stays flagged and is the same occurrence again then, and preview_reopen lists each of these per occurrence.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A real payday never goes without its pay-date transfer: every period has a scheduled pay date of its own as its key, the next one no period has when the projected one is taken, so several salaries in one month give as many occurrences, the same keys through a reopen and the salary recorded again, and each occurrence is listed once, in the period that plans it, whatever its key.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), M1 with C1, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Deleting a budget, or its owner's login, never fails because of its transfers: the transfers' bookkeeping (looking at the plan again, an income gone, a transaction's mark) does nothing while the budget itself is being deleted, also within the transaction that created it; any refusal is a named code (P0001).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), M2 with C5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Moving a period's start moves the automatic transfer transactions the app recorded by itself to their new due date, in the right period, as a reopen and the salary recorded that day would; a member's own mark stays where the member put it, and the move's preview counts what moves.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), M3, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A pay-date transfer that names the income that is the primary income (in the periods since it became primary) behaves exactly as one that names no income: keyed by the scheduled pay date, due when the salary actually came, and never said to follow the primary instead.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), S1, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Ending the income a pay-date transfer chose (remove_income, remove_member, leave_budget in the current period) never rewrites what is already recorded: its occurrences of that period already due that day stay with their marks and transactions, and the transfer follows the primary income from the next occurrence not yet due, so nothing dated in the past appears.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), S2, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A reopen keeps a transfer that has a mark even when it would then be in force nowhere: it stays, listed as ended with its marks and their transactions until undone, and preview_reopen says it is ended (not removed) and that each such mark is no longer planned.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), S3, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: preview_reopen takes the same optional pay date as the reopen and describes that reopen, also when the reopen at its default end would be refused.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), S4, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A fixed-day transfer's next due date is found 13 months ahead, so a yearly or quarterly transfer shows it all year.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), S5, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Creating a transfer records nothing dated before today unless the member asks for it by naming the period or a first date; then the preview says what is created at once.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), C3, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: One catch-up step creates at most a bounded number of transactions per budget (4000, and about two seconds of work), leaving the rest due, none skipped; a step that stops before creating every one due never answers 0 from ensure_periods.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The structured spec is the source of truth
decisions.decision: spec/spec.json holds the glossary, actors, features and user stories, rules, decisions, conventions and open questions. docs/spec.md and the conventions block of CLAUDE.md are generated from it, and npm run spec:check fails when the spec, its tests or its generated views disagree.
decisions.why: Prose cannot be checked; a structured file with ids lets code that breaks a rule be caught early.
rejected: Keeping docs/domain.md as the prose source of truth: readable, but nothing can check it.
Hand-maintained copies of the rules in several files: they drift.

decisions.title: docs/domain.md is the source of truth for product behaviour
decisions.decision: docs/domain.md recorded the product owner's requirements and the decisions taken on top of them, updated when a decision changed.
decisions.why: One readable place for product behaviour.

decisions.title: Static single-page app on Supabase, no custom server
decisions.decision: The app is a static SPA (Vite, React, TypeScript strict, Tailwind, shadcn/ui) that calls Supabase (Postgres, Auth, RLS) directly from the browser with supabase-js. No Node and no PHP at runtime.
decisions.why: Any static host can serve the build, and access control lives in one place: RLS.
rejected: A custom server or API in front of the database.
Running Node or PHP on the hosting.

decisions.title: Infomaniak static hosting with an .htaccess SPA fallback
decisions.decision: dist/ is served as static files by Infomaniak Apache web hosting. public/.htaccess serves index.html for unknown paths, but a missing file under assets/ is a real 404, and every module-specific block is wrapped in <IfModule>.
decisions.why: Deep links and reloads work; serving HTML in place of a missing script would hide the error behind a MIME type failure; a missing module must not turn the site into a 500.
rejected: Serving index.html for missing assets.

decisions.title: Manual deploy workflow, gated by the CI checks
decisions.decision: The Deploy GitHub workflow runs only when started by hand. It checks the variables and the CSP, runs lint, typecheck and tests, builds, and syncs dist/ to the site folder with rsync over SSH. A rollback is a deploy of an earlier ref.
decisions.why: A manual run on a broken ref cannot ship it; the server keeps its .well-known folder.

decisions.title: Migrations go out before the code and stay backwards compatible
decisions.decision: Migrations are pushed to the hosted project before deploying a release that needs them, and are kept compatible with the previous release (add first, remove in a later release), or fixed forward.
decisions.why: The new code never runs against an old schema, and a rollback does not undo migrations.
rejected: Relying on a rollback to undo a migration.

decisions.title: Money is integer rappen
decisions.decision: Amounts are integer rappen (1 CHF = 100 rappen) in the database (bigint) and in code (a safe integer number), and are formatted only at the edge.
decisions.why: Exact arithmetic.
rejected: Floats.

decisions.title: CHF only
decisions.decision: The app handles one currency, the Swiss franc.
decisions.why: A household budget in Switzerland.

decisions.title: Swiss money format, the same in both languages
decisions.decision: Amounts are shown as "CHF 1'234.50" (apostrophe for thousands, dot for rappen, sign before the digits: "CHF -12.00"), whatever the UI language. Input accepts an optional CHF, a sign, ' or ’ or spaces between thousands, a dot or a comma with at most two decimals, and the Swiss ".-" for whole francs.
decisions.why: The source asks for Swiss formatting; one format avoids ambiguity between languages.

decisions.title: Two kinds of date, one formatter each
decisions.decision: Calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and timestamps (with a time and an explicit zone) each have their own formatter, and each rejects the other kind and any invalid input with a RangeError. Typed dates are dd.mm.yyyy, one-digit day and month allowed.
decisions.why: They cannot be mixed up at a call site, and an invalid input never prints a plausible-looking wrong date.
rejected: A single formatter that guesses the kind of value.

decisions.title: Tests run in Europe/Zurich
decisions.decision: Vitest runs with TZ=Europe/Zurich.
decisions.why: A non-UTC zone with summer time makes time-zone shifts visible in tests.
rejected: Running tests in UTC, where shifts go unnoticed.

decisions.title: Auth email links use the implicit flow
decisions.decision: supabase-js is configured with flowType implicit: confirmation and password-reset links carry the session in the URL fragment.
decisions.why: Links then also work when opened in another browser or on another device.
rejected: PKCE: it needs the code verifier stored by the browser that requested the email.

decisions.title: The app reads email links itself and replaces the history entry
decisions.decision: detectSessionInUrl is off. At start-up, before the router or the Supabase client sees the URL, the app takes tokens or errors out of the URL by replacing the current history entry, and the auth bootstrap hands the tokens to supabase-js.
decisions.why: supabase-js clears the fragment with location.hash = "", which pushes a new history entry and leaves the token-bearing URL one Back step away.
rejected: Letting supabase-js detect the session in the URL.

decisions.title: Recovery mode is tied to one sign-in
decisions.decision: The recovery flag in localStorage names the user and the session key of the sign-in the recovery link created; recovery mode is active only while that exact session is current. Tabs learn of changes through the storage event.
decisions.why: It never applies to another user, nor to the same user after a fresh password sign-in, and a leftover flag is inert even before it is cleaned up. Every tab sharing the session sees it.
rejected: A flag that is not tied to one sign-in, which would hold another user or a later password sign-in on the form.

decisions.title: Undecided link tokens are parked for one tab
decisions.decision: Until the bootstrap has a definite answer for link tokens, they are kept in sessionStorage (this tab only, never in a URL or history entry), for at most 24 hours, together with the session key current when they were parked. A reload retries them only if nobody signed in or out in between.
decisions.why: A network failure while validating a link must not burn it.
rejected: Dropping the link on a network failure.
Keeping the tokens in the URL.

decisions.title: Session identity from the unverified session_id claim
decisions.decision: A sign-in is identified by the session_id claim of its access token (stable across refreshes, new with every sign-in), or by the user id when there is none. The token payload is decoded without verifying its signature.
decisions.why: It is used only to tell sessions apart in this browser, never to grant access: the server checks every request.

decisions.title: Clear the query cache when the user changes
decisions.decision: The TanStack Query cache is cleared whenever the signed-in user changes, including sign-out.
decisions.why: Never show one user's cached data to another.

decisions.title: Zod runs jitless
decisions.decision: z.config({ jitless: true }) runs before any schema is parsed.
decisions.why: The production CSP forbids eval; Zod's probe for new Function is caught, but the browser still reports a CSP violation.
rejected: Zod's default probe and compiled parsers.

decisions.title: Validation messages are translation keys
decisions.decision: Form schemas return translation keys; forms translate them when rendering. Passwords need 8 characters, display names at most 80.
decisions.why: The language can change while an error is shown.

decisions.title: Language detection
decisions.decision: The UI language is the stored choice, else the browser language, reduced to en or fr ("fr-CH" -> "fr"), with English as the fallback. French text uses a narrow no-break space before ? ! : and ;.
decisions.why: Respect an explicit choice, then the browser.

decisions.title: Email confirmation stays on in production
decisions.decision: Email confirmation is kept on for production, with a custom SMTP server for real use.
decisions.why: The free tier sender sends only a few emails per hour.

decisions.title: Narrow connect-src to the project, checked at deploy
decisions.decision: The CSP connect-src should list only the project URL (https and wss); the Deploy workflow stops before building when VITE_SUPABASE_URL is not allowed by connect-src, and checks the policy that actually ships.
decisions.why: The browser may only talk to origins the CSP allows.

decisions.title: Domain logic is pure and unit-tested in the client
decisions.decision: Period, pay-date and versioning logic is pure and unit-tested.
decisions.why: Testable logic.

decisions.title: Domain logic has one implementation, in the database
decisions.decision: Period, pay-date and versioning logic has one implementation, in the database (SQL functions, tested with pgTAP). The client reads the results; it never recomputes them.
decisions.why: One implementation cannot disagree with itself; the database must enforce the invariants anyway.
rejected: A second implementation in the client (D-023).

decisions.title: Periods are numbered; versions refer to period numbers
decisions.decision: Periods are numbered per budget (seq 1, 2, ...). Income validity (first_seq, end_seq) and versions (effective_from_seq) refer to seq, not to dates. An income counts in period p when first_seq <= p and (end_seq is null or p < end_seq), at the version with the greatest effective_from_seq <= p.
decisions.why: Moving a period boundary never changes which version applies.
rejected: Versions effective from a date.

decisions.title: "Today" comes from one database function
decisions.decision: A database function returns the Europe/Zurich calendar date; it is the only source of the current date, and the browser never sends "today". Tests pin it by replacing the function inside their transaction.
decisions.why: One clock for every rule that depends on the date.
rejected: The browser's clock.
UTC.

decisions.title: Writes go through RPCs with stable error codes
decisions.decision: Writes that touch several rows or carry invariants go through security definer RPCs that check membership themselves. The client writes directly only budgets.name and incomes.name (members) and deletes budgets and invitations (owner). RPC errors are SQLSTATE P0001 with a stable snake_case message that the client maps to translated text.
decisions.why: Invariants are enforced in one place; the client can translate every error.

decisions.title: Not found, never forbidden
decisions.decision: A request for a budget, income, period or invitation the caller cannot see is answered as not found; reads of rows outside one's budgets return no rows, never an error.
decisions.why: Non-members cannot tell a budget they may not see from one that does not exist.

decisions.title: Limits
decisions.decision: At most 20 owned budgets per user, 20 members per budget, 20 pending invitations per budget, 50 incomes per budget (ended ones included). Income amounts from 1 to 1 000 000 000 rappen. A budget starts at most 60 months back; an end date at most ten years ahead; a period is never empty and at most 70 days long. The limits are defined in one place in the migration.
decisions.why: Bound the work of every RPC and keep abuse cheap.

decisions.title: An income that never counted is deleted, not ended
decisions.decision: Removing an income deletes it if it never counted in a past period, and otherwise ends it from the current period. The same applies to the incomes of a member who is removed or leaves.
decisions.why: An income added by mistake leaves no trace; history is kept otherwise.

decisions.title: The primary income also blocks leaving
decisions.decision: A member whose income is the primary income can neither be removed nor leave until another income is made primary.
decisions.why: The budget must keep a primary income.

decisions.title: An end date snaps forward to a period end
decisions.decision: Setting an end date moves it forward to the end of the period that contains it, projected with the primary income's current terms. Clearing it resumes period generation. An end date that would delete existing periods is refused, and a boundary that is the budget's end date is changed through the end date.
decisions.why: The end date always falls on a period boundary without deleting history.

decisions.title: Invitations are idempotent per address
decisions.decision: Inviting the same address again returns the same invitation; addresses are stored lower case; inviting a member's address is refused (already_member).
decisions.why: Members' emails are visible to the owner anyway, so already_member reveals nothing new.

decisions.title: Database conventions
decisions.decision: Functions the API must not call live in the private schema, which the Data API does not expose. Functions use search_path = '' and schema-qualified names. Privileges are granted explicitly (auto_expose_new_tables = false): revoke everything from the API roles, then grant only what the policies allow. Policies call (select auth.uid()).
decisions.why: Nothing is exposed by accident, and auth.uid() is evaluated once per statement.

decisions.title: Shared membership helpers
decisions.decision: Policies use private.member_budget_ids() and private.owned_budget_ids() as `budget_id in (select ...)`; the helpers are security definer.
decisions.why: The helper runs once per statement and never re-enters the policies of budget_members (no recursion).
rejected: Re-deriving membership in every policy.

decisions.title: Invariants are constraint triggers checked at commit
decisions.decision: Invariants (owner is a member, primary income is active, every income has a version from its first period, periods numbered and contiguous up to the end date) are constraint triggers checked at commit.
decisions.why: Multi-row RPCs can pass through intermediate states.

decisions.title: Period creation is serialised per budget
decisions.decision: Every function that creates or moves periods first locks the budget row; ensure_periods is idempotent and safe under concurrent calls.
decisions.why: Concurrent callers run one after the other and cannot create duplicate periods.

decisions.title: Deferred: 13th salary and one-off incomes
decisions.decision: Incomes are monthly for now; a 13th salary or a one-off income comes later.
decisions.why: Not needed for the first version.

decisions.title: Deferred: per-category rollover
decisions.decision: Category balances reset at the end of each period; per-category rollover may come later as an opt-in.
decisions.why: Keep the first version simple.

decisions.title: No bank connection; actuals may be overlaid later
decisions.decision: The money flow diagram is drawn from the plan. The app has no bank connection, so it does not depend on detecting automatic transactions. Actuals may be overlaid later.
decisions.why: No bank integration.
rejected: Detecting automatic transactions from a bank feed.
source: domain: Account and planned transfer (money flow)

decisions.title: Deferred: import from a connector
decisions.decision: Import is reachable from a paste/CSV screen and a repository script first, and later from a connector.
decisions.why: Ship the two paths that need no extra integration first.
source: domain: Import (including by a Claude session)

decisions.title: Temporary "test pending" marker for untagged database tests
decisions.decision: A rule or convention whose proof lives in supabase/tests may carry a visible testPending marker until those tests are tagged with ids. spec:check reports every marker as a warning, with a count, and errors on a marker anywhere else (planned rule, enforcement other than test).
decisions.why: The database tests were being edited by another developer when the spec was introduced; the check must pass without silently passing or weakening those rules.
rejected: Silently treating untagged rules as covered.
Downgrading them to enforcement review.

decisions.title: Profiles are created by a database trigger
decisions.decision: A trigger on auth.users creates the profile at sign-up from the display name sent as sign-up metadata. Clients cannot insert or delete profiles; deleting the user cascades.
decisions.why: Every user has a profile without a client round trip.

decisions.title: Deploying in a subfolder
decisions.decision: VITE_BASE_PATH sets both Vite's base and the router basename at build time; .htaccess works out the base path itself.
decisions.why: The same build works at a domain root or in a subfolder.

decisions.title: Members manage every income of the budget
decisions.decision: Any member of a budget can add, edit and remove any income in that budget, including one belonging to another member. A new income belongs to the member who adds it by default; the form lets them choose another member. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-15.
decisions.why: It matches "every member can read and edit everything in the budget" and what the database already does.
rejected: Members can only add and edit their own incomes.
source: owner-request: product owner decision on Q-001, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: The current budget is a per-user browser preference
decisions.decision: The budget a user works in is kept in localStorage under a key that names the user; when it is missing or no longer in my_budgets, the first budget by name is used (and not stored until the user chooses). my_budgets is refetched on window focus and after any "not found" answer. Users without a budget are routed to /welcome; app pages require a budget.
decisions.why: Reloads keep the choice, two people sharing a browser keep their own, and a budget that disappears is replaced at once.
rejected: Storing the choice in the database: a per-browser convenience, not budget data.
Putting the budget id in every URL: longer links and more routing for a household app.

decisions.title: One mutation pattern with one error mapping
decisions.decision: Writes go through useAppMutation: pending state, a translated success toast, the error either inline (forms, dialogs) or as a toast (one-click actions), and invalidation of the affected queries (everything of a budget sits under ["budget", id]). Errors are mapped in src/lib/db-errors.ts only, with a generic translated fallback, and a call may word some codes its own way (for example "already deleted" for delete_budget); the list of codes is checked against the contract's error table; a "not found" answer is always toasted and refetches my budgets.
decisions.why: Later features copy one pattern; a new error code is one line plus its two translations.

decisions.title: Day N of M uses the browser's date, display only
decisions.decision: The dashboard's "day N of M" counts calendar days from the current period's start to the browser's local date, clamped to the period. Which period is current, its dates and its totals come from the database. To be replaced if the contract provides today (Q-016).
decisions.why: The contract gives no "today"; the number is cosmetic and never sent back.

decisions.title: One period per calendar month
decisions.decision: Each period belongs to one calendar month (periods.month) and starts on that month's salary (anchor_date, the scheduled actual pay date). Consecutive periods have consecutive months. A period's projected end is the day before the actual pay date of the next month's nominal pay day under the terms in force for the next period. A mid-period change of the primary's pay day or weekend rule therefore applies to the next month's pay date.
decisions.why: An early salary, a close-by nominal date or a pay-day change could otherwise cut a period short and count a month's salary twice.
rejected: Projecting the end from the first pay date after the period start: an early salary created a 2-day period and a second salary in the same month (review finding 1).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: A manual boundary lies within 14 days of its salary
decisions.decision: A boundary set by hand must leave the next period starting within 14 days of the scheduled pay date of its month. This bound replaces the 70-day period length limit as the abuse limit.
decisions.why: It covers public holidays and late or early salaries, and stops repeated early closes from creating periods without salaries.
rejected: A maximum period length of 70 days: allowed several 1-day periods each with the full income.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: No period starts after today
decisions.decision: Periods exist only up to the one containing today. Moving the boundary before the latest period to today or later means the salary has not arrived yet: the latest period is removed and the previous one is current again with that end. Moving any earlier boundary to today or later is refused.
decisions.why: A future period made an earlier one current again and let an edit be written to a closed period while the next one kept stale terms (review finding 2).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Every manual boundary operation has an inverse
decisions.decision: move_period_boundary(period, null) resets the boundary after a period to the schedule; any move can be moved back. Closing a period early is undone by moving or resetting that boundary, which removes the period started early if its salary is still to come.
decisions.why: One-way operations any member can trigger turn a mistake into permanent damage.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Writing a version discards later versions
decisions.decision: Writing a version for period s deletes the versions of the same entity keyed to later periods, through one generic trigger (private.discard_later_versions) that every versioned table (incomes now; categories, subscriptions and debts later) uses.
decisions.why: A version left for a later period (after a late salary removed that period) would otherwise shadow the edit just saved.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Explicit corrections of the past are allowed, implicit ones never
decisions.decision: Normal edits and removals apply from the current period. update_income_terms and remove_income take an optional from-period (default current) so a mistake, including a back-dated one, can be corrected or the income removed from the period it started in (which deletes it).
decisions.why: A back-dated typo otherwise stayed in every past total for good (review finding 3a).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Limits (revised)
decisions.decision: At most 20 owned budgets per user, 20 members per budget, 20 pending (unexpired) invitations per budget, 50 incomes in force and 500 incomes in all per budget. Income amounts from 1 to 1 000 000 000 rappen. A budget starts at most 60 months back; an end date at most ten years ahead. A manual boundary lies within 14 days of its salary (D-061). The limits are defined in one place in the migration.
decisions.why: Counting ended incomes made the income limit a lifetime limit (review finding 3b); the period-length limit did not stop abuse (D-061).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: The end date is a final month
decisions.decision: A budget stores its final month (end_month). Setting an end date picks the month whose period contains it; the end date shown is that period's end (projected while it does not exist), so it follows later changes of the terms and is always a normal boundary. The final boundary is adjusted like any other, in one call. An end date that would delete existing periods is refused.
decisions.why: A stored end date became a stub period with a full month's income when the terms changed (review finding 10).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Invitations expire and name the inviter
decisions.decision: Invitations expire 30 days after they were last sent; re-inviting renews the same invitation. list_my_invitations returns the inviter's name and email. Invitation security depends on Supabase Auth "Confirm email" staying on in the hosted project (docs/deployment.md).
decisions.why: A display name is chosen by its owner and proves nothing; an invitation should not stay valid for ever.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Budget writes take an advisory lock; reads take none
decisions.decision: Every RPC that changes a budget's periods, incomes or members takes a transaction-level advisory lock for the budget and only then reads the rows it checks. ensure_periods and get_current_period take no lock when there is nothing to create. Accepting an invitation locks the invitation row.
decisions.why: A row lock on the budget blocked page loads behind any transaction inserting rows of the budget (review finding 6); reading before locking gave raw errors and let a cancelled invitation be accepted (findings 4 and 7).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: The database gives "today" and the start months
decisions.decision: period_summaries (and so get_current_period) carry the database's today; get_today() returns it on its own; get_start_months(pay day, weekend rule) returns today and the valid start months with the date each first period would start.
decisions.why: The client must never use the browser's clock for what the database decides (Q-016).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: create_budget takes the end date
decisions.decision: create_budget has an optional end date, applied in the same transaction.
decisions.why: A second call could fail and leave a budget without the end date the user asked for (Q-017).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Deletes go through RPCs that say why
decisions.decision: Deleting a budget and cancelling an invitation are RPCs (delete_budget, cancel_invitation) that answer budget_not_found / invitation_not_found or not_owner; the client has no direct delete privilege on these tables.
decisions.why: A direct delete affecting no rows cannot tell "not allowed" from "already gone".
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: A manual end survives a terms change only within 14 days
decisions.decision: When the primary's terms change or the primary is switched, a manual end of the current period is kept while it lies within 14 days of the new schedule, and reset to the schedule otherwise.
decisions.why: Keeping it unconditionally would let the next period start more than 14 days from its salary (D-061).
rejected: Refusing the terms change: blocks the user for a boundary they may have forgotten.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Profiles carry the email and stay readable for income labels
decisions.decision: profiles.email mirrors the account email (trigger on auth.users). Members can read the profiles of co-members and of anyone with an income in their budgets.
decisions.why: Member lists show emails; a former member's ended income must keep its owner's name.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Periods are salary to salary; stored periods are facts
decisions.decision: A period runs from one salary to the day before the next. Stored periods are facts: only the boundary operations move a stored boundary. The schedule (the primary income's pay day and weekend rule) only predicts the next pay date. Structural invariants only, none depending on terms: contiguous, non-overlapping, none starting after today or after the budget's end date, each 7 to 92 days long. Known limits of the model: a first salary arriving 8 to 14 days after a period started is skipped by the projection until recorded by hand (record_early_pay_date); two salaries closer than 7 days cannot be separate periods.
decisions.why: The month anchor and the 14-day rule (D-060, D-061) tied stored periods to the terms currently in force: budgets got stuck (every period call failing) and real pay-day changes, such as from the 5th to the 25th within one month, could not be represented.
rejected: One period per calendar month within 14 days of its scheduled salary (D-060, D-061): see why.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16
