decisions.title: The projection rule
decisions.decision: The next pay date after a period is the first actual pay date, under the primary income's terms in force, at least 15 days after the period's start; the projected end is the day before. When re-projecting because terms changed, the next pay date must also be after today, so the current period stays current. One pure function (private.next_salary_date).
decisions.why: Periods generated this way are never shorter than 15 days, an early salary never creates a stub, and a change of terms never closes a period retroactively.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Boundary operations, each with an inverse
decisions.decision: Four operations: set_expected_pay_date (the current period's end, after today; null resets it to the projection); record_early_pay_date (the salary arrived early: the next period starts on a date up to today); reopen_previous_period (the salary has not arrived yet: the latest period is merged into the previous one, which ends before a future date or at its projection; the inverse of an early close); move_period_start (moves the boundary between two existing periods to a date up to today; undone by moving it back). Every write RPC catches the periods up to today first. The length bounds are the abuse limit.
decisions.why: Each real-life case has one clear operation, and each has an inverse.
rejected: One move_period_boundary operation whose meaning depended on the period's position: hard to use and to undo.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Merging the latest period re-keys what was keyed to it
decisions.decision: When the latest period is merged into the previous one, everything keyed to it (income versions, incomes starting or ending there, and so the primary switch) is re-keyed to the previous period, the later write winning. Nothing is ever keyed beyond the latest period (constraint trigger). One shared mechanism: private.rekey_period over the registry private.period_keyed_tables, which later versioned tables (categories, subscriptions, debts) join.
decisions.why: A change made "now" must always be in force now; the discard-later-versions mechanism (D-064) is no longer needed.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A correction applies until the next change
decisions.decision: A correction from period K writes the version at K and leaves later versions alone: it applies from K until the next existing change.
decisions.why: Correcting one early period rewrote every later period (review finding 3).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Limits (revised again)
decisions.decision: At most 20 owned budgets per user, 20 members per budget, 20 pending (unexpired) invitations per budget, 50 incomes in force and 500 incomes in all per budget. Income amounts from 1 to 1 000 000 000 rappen. A budget starts at most 60 months back; an end date at most ten years ahead. A period is 7 to 92 days long (generated periods at least 15 by construction). The limits are defined in one place in the migration.
decisions.why: The 14-day rule is gone (D-080); the length bounds are the abuse limit for boundary operations.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The budget end is the date entered
decisions.decision: The budget stores the end date the owner entered. No period starts after it; the period containing it is the last and ends at its normal projected end. The end shown (my_budgets.end_date) is that period's end and follows later term changes by itself; it can be adjusted like the current period's end.
decisions.why: A stored final month tied the end to the calendar-month model (D-067).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: One lock order
decisions.decision: Every RPC takes the budget's advisory lock before any row lock; accept_invitation, decline_invitation and cancel_invitation included.
decisions.why: accept_invitation locked the invitation row before the budget while invite_member did the opposite, which deadlocked (review finding 4).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A former member keeps only their name
decisions.decision: Members read the profiles (name and email) of people who share a budget with them now. A former member's income keeps its owner's display name through income_overview.user_display_name only.
decisions.why: A later joiner could read the email of a former member they never shared the budget with (review finding 5).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A yearly amount shows as one twelfth, rounded to the rappen
decisions.decision: A yearly amount is stored as yearly. The monthly figure shown is one twelfth of it, rounded to the nearest rappen. The twelve monthly shares are not required to add up exactly to the yearly amount. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-002. A simple, predictable monthly figure matters more than a few rappen of difference over a year.
rejected: Spreading the remainder over some months so that twelve shares add up exactly to the yearly amount.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Left to assign is per period
decisions.decision: The amount left to assign for a period is that period's income total minus the sum of the category expectations in force in that period. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-003. Incomes and expectations are both versioned per period, so the two sides of the subtraction must come from the same period.
rejected: The monthly total of the incomes in force now.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Transactions are positive expenses, with a refund option, on the lowest level
decisions.decision: A transaction is an expense entered as a positive amount. A "refund" option records money coming back; a refund reduces what was spent in its category. When a category has subcategories, a transaction goes on a subcategory, never on the parent category. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-004. Users enter what they paid as they see it on the receipt; tracking happens where the expectations are set (R-CATEGORY-002).
rejected: Signed amounts, with a negative amount for money coming back.
Transactions directly on a category that has subcategories.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A period's result is income minus spending
decisions.decision: A period's result is its income total minus the total spent in it: a surplus when positive, a deficit when negative. Per category, the result is the expected amount minus what was spent. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-012. It tells the household whether it lived within its income, whatever was assigned.
rejected: Measuring the period's result against the sum of its expectations.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Browsing past periods is part of step 3
decisions.decision: Browsing a past period and seeing its progress view belongs to step 3 (period progress view). The comparison charts stay in step 5. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-010. A past period's progress view is the same view as the current one; only the charts are new work.
rejected: Browsing past periods only with the comparison charts of step 5.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: What stays editable in a past period
decisions.decision: In a past period, transactions can be added, edited and deleted freely. Its boundaries are changed through the period actions. Incomes and category expectations are changed only through the explicit "correct an earlier period" option. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-011. Late receipts and corrections of what was spent are normal; changing the plan of a past period must be deliberate.
rejected: Only transactions are editable in a past period.
Everything in a past period is editable freely.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Overspending and over-assigning are never blocked
decisions.decision: Overspending a category and assigning more than the income are never blocked. An overspent category is shown as overspent; assigning more than the income shows a negative amount left to assign. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: The app records what happens and shows it; it does not stop the household from recording reality or planning.
rejected: Refusing a transaction or an expectation that goes over the limit.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Categories end like incomes; expectations are versioned like incomes
decisions.decision: Deleting a category that has transactions or has counted in a past period ends it from the current period and keeps it in past periods, like incomes (D-030); one that has neither is deleted. Category expectations are versioned like incomes: an edit applies from the current period, with the same optional "correct an earlier period" (D-065). Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Past periods must keep showing what was planned and spent in them.
rejected: Deleting a category together with its transactions and its history.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Subscription cadences and charge dates
decisions.decision: Subscription cadences are monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and yearly. A subscription has a first charge date and then repeats on the same day of the month, clamped to the month's length. No weekend rule applies to subscriptions. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-006. Providers charge on a calendar day, weekends included.
rejected: Applying the incomes' weekend rule to subscription charges.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Subscription charges are recorded automatically and confirmed on the dashboard
decisions.decision: On its charge date, a subscription's transaction is created automatically, marked as coming from the subscription, and can be edited or deleted. The dashboard shows a notification for each such automatic charge asking the user to confirm that it really went through; until confirmed it is marked as awaiting confirmation. The user can instead say it did not go through, which removes it. Assumption (not asked of the product owner): a charge awaiting confirmation counts in totals immediately, like imported transactions (D-118). Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Recurring charges should not have to be typed in, but a failed or cancelled charge must not stay in the budget unnoticed.
rejected: Entering subscription charges by hand.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A subscription is committed inside its category
decisions.decision: A subscription's monthly cost is shown as "committed" inside its category's expectation, not added on top of it. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: The category's expectation stays the whole plan for that kind of spending; the subscription shows how much of it is already spoken for.
rejected: Adding subscriptions on top of the category expectations.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A transaction links to at most one of a debt or a subscription
decisions.decision: A transaction links to at most one of a debt or a subscription. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-005.
rejected: Linking a transaction to both a debt and a subscription.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Debts belong to a category; payments are transactions
decisions.decision: A debt is tied to a category. A payment is a normal transaction in that category, linked to the debt. Only debts the household owes are tracked, not money owed to it. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Debt payments are spending like any other and must count in the budget without being entered twice.
rejected: Tracking money owed to the household as well.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Remaining amount, interest and expected end of a debt
decisions.decision: A debt's remaining amount is the principal plus accrued interest minus the payments linked to it. When the debt has an interest rate, once per period one twelfth of the yearly rate is applied to the remaining balance and added to it, and shown in the debt's history. The expected end date is projected from the planned monthly payment; when the payment does not cover the interest, the app says the debt never ends. A manual "adjust balance" entry lets the user match their bank statement. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-007. A simple model the user can check against the bank, with an escape hatch when the bank computes differently.
rejected: Remaining amount as the principal minus the payments, ignoring interest.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The comparison charts
decisions.decision: Step 5 has these charts: income, spent and result per period over the last 12 periods; spending per category across periods; and two periods side by side. The product owner leaves latitude to include anything else that brings value to the user, and sets a quality bar: keep it beautiful. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: These answer the household's questions: how are we doing over the year, where does the money go, what changed.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: What an import duplicate is
decisions.decision: An imported row is a duplicate when it has the same date, amount and description as an existing transaction, or the same bank transaction id when the file has one. Duplicates are skipped and listed in the import summary, with an "import anyway" option. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-009. Re-importing an overlapping export must not double the spending, but two genuine identical purchases must still be possible.
rejected: Silently dropping duplicates with no way to import them.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The import script authenticates with an import token
decisions.decision: The script a Claude session runs authenticates with an import token the user creates in Settings. A token is tied to one budget, can only add transactions through the import function (it cannot read anything), and can be revoked. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-013. Claude never gets raw database access to real data (R-SECURITY-005), nor the member's own credentials.
rejected: The script signs in as the member.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Merchant rules are offered in one click
decisions.decision: When the user categorises an imported transaction, the app offers "always put this merchant in this category?" with one click. The rules are editable in Settings. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-014. The user stays in control of the rules, at the cost of one click.
rejected: Saving a rule automatically whenever an imported transaction is categorised.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Imported transactions count at once and wait for review
decisions.decision: Imported transactions count in totals immediately and are flagged "to review" until the user confirms them. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Totals stay close to reality right after an import, and the flag still shows what has not been checked.
rejected: Leaving imported transactions out of the totals until they are reviewed.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Generic CSV import plus presets for the household's sources
decisions.decision: The import offers a generic CSV import with column mapping, plus presets for the product owner's sources: Migros Bank, Raiffeisen, One, Yuh and Twint. Which product "One" is and what each source exports are open (Q-058). Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Any bank's export can be imported, and the household's own sources need no mapping.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: How a planned transfer is scheduled
decisions.decision: A planned transfer is scheduled either as an offset in days from a chosen income's actual pay date (the primary income by default), or on a fixed day of the month. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-008. Members are paid on different days, and some transfers follow the calendar rather than a salary.
rejected: Always counting from the primary income's pay date (the period start).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Planned transfers are versioned like incomes
decisions.decision: Planned transfers are versioned like incomes: an edit applies from the current period. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-015. Past periods' checklists and flows keep showing the plan that was in force.
rejected: Edits to a planned transfer rewrite every period.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A planned transfer can create its transaction in a category
decisions.decision: A planned transfer can be linked to a category (for example savings, third pillar, taxes). When it is marked done, or when it is automatic, the transaction is created in that category, so it is not entered twice. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Transfers to savings, the third pillar or the tax reserve are part of the budget; recording them once avoids double entry.
rejected: Entering the transfer's transaction by hand as well.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: No account balances
decisions.decision: Account balances are not tracked; the money flow diagram shows flows only. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: The app has no bank connection (D-040); balances kept by hand would drift from the bank's.
rejected: Tracking a balance per account.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Concurrent edits: the second save is refused
decisions.decision: When two members edit the same thing at the same time, the second save is refused with a message that it was changed by someone else and must be reloaded. This applies to every editable record, starting with incomes. It is implemented with step 3, for the existing step 2 records as well. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-018. Every member can edit everything (D-045); silently losing another member's change is worse than asking to reload.
rejected: The last write wins without a warning (the step 2 behaviour).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Account deletion comes after step 7
decisions.decision: There is no account deletion until after step 7. When it is built, an owner must first transfer ownership of their budgets or delete them, and a member deleting their account counts as leaving the budget. Until then, R-BUDGET-016 records the database behaviour only; no client path deletes accounts. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-030. Deleting the owner's account must not delete a budget other members rely on, and a deleted member's incomes must follow the leaving rules (R-MEMBER-007, R-MEMBER-009).
rejected: Deleting the owner's account deletes their budgets for every member.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: In a merge, the merged period always wins
decisions.decision: When the latest period is merged into the previous one, everything keyed to the merged (later) period is re-keyed to the previous one and replaces what the previous period had for the same record, whatever the write times. So the terms in force before a reopen are still in force after it. Nothing is ever keyed beyond the latest period. One shared mechanism (private.rekey_period over private.period_keyed_tables). What the reopened period loses can be listed beforehand (preview_reopen). The inverse of a reopen (record_early_pay_date with the original date) restores the boundary only: what was recorded in the merged period then belongs to the reopened period, and moving it back needs explicit corrections.
decisions.why: "The later write wins" let a correction of the previous period, written after a raise in the new period, undo the raise; re-keyed versions got fresh write times and beat later corrections (review finding 1).
rejected: The later write wins (D-083).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Removing a member from an ended budget takes effect if it resumes
decisions.decision: Removing a member (or a member leaving) after the budget has ended leaves its history as it is and marks their incomes in force (incomes.ended_after_last); if the budget ever resumes, they end from the first period created after the end.
decisions.why: Nothing may be keyed beyond the latest period, yet the removal must hold when an owner clears the end date (review finding 2).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: What a period-keyed table must provide
decisions.decision: A table registers in private.period_keyed_tables, checked at registration: all need id uuid and budget_id uuid; validity tables first_seq integer, end_seq integer, a text name column and a check allowing end_seq = first_seq; version tables an entity column (uuid) referencing a registered validity table, effective_from_seq integer and a unique constraint on (entity, effective_from_seq). In a merge, a validity row that would never be in force is deleted, or kept as a void row (end_seq = first_seq, never in force) when other rows reference it, so a reopen never fails on a foreign key.
decisions.why: Step 3 registers categories, which transactions reference; the merge must neither fail at reopen time nor silently need columns nobody documented (review finding 4).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Previews before writes
decisions.decision: preview_reopen lists, from the registry, every change a reopen would move (record kind, id, name, added / ended / removed / terms_changed / made_primary, and whether it replaces the previous period's own entry). preview_expected_pay_date gives the current period's end and expected pay date for proposed terms or a proposed primary, through the same function the write uses (private.reprojected_end).
decisions.why: The UI must be able to warn before a lossy reopen and show the effect of a pay-day change before it is saved.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rejected: Rounding the exact sum of the yearly amounts: the total would differ from the sum of the figures shown.
Banker's rounding: unfamiliar, for no benefit at this size.
decisions.title: A half rappen rounds up; totals add the rounded shares
decisions.decision: One twelfth of a yearly amount is rounded half up to the rappen. A total shown for a period (expected, left to assign, results) adds the rounded monthly shares, so what is displayed adds up. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-050. A user adding up the monthly figures on screen gets the total shown.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rejected: Refusing the first subcategory while the category has transactions: the user would have to move them by hand.
Turning a group back into a leaf when its last subcategory goes: open as Q-081.
decisions.title: The first subcategory makes a group; what the category held moves to "Other"
decisions.decision: A category becomes a group (categories.is_group) when its first subcategory is created, and stays one. When it already had transactions or a non-zero expectation, those, with every past expectation version, move to a subcategory created with it, named by the client (shown as "Other"), valid from the category's first period. A group holds no expectation and no transaction; its figures are the sums of its subcategories'. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-051. No transaction is ever left on a category that has subcategories (D-102), past periods keep their totals, and a category that stays a group keeps one shape across its history.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rejected: Comparing updated_at timestamps: two writes in one transaction share a timestamp.
Requiring the revision on step 2 RPCs at once: the deployed client would fail until the frontend ships.
decisions.title: Concurrent edits: one revision per record
decisions.decision: Every editable record (budget, income, category, transaction, and every later one) has an integer revision, raised by a trigger whenever its row changes and explicitly when a dependent row changes (an income's terms, a category's expectation). Every edit or removal RPC takes p_expected_revision and refuses with record_changed when it differs; the write RPCs take the budget lock first, so a second save waits for the first and then sees the new revision. Step 3 RPCs require it (invalid_revision when missing). Step 2's update_income_terms, remove_income and set_budget_end_date take it as an optional last argument, and the direct renames of budgets and incomes stay, so the previous release keeps working (D-006); new rename_budget and rename_income RPCs check it. A later release makes it required and revokes the direct renames. Reordering categories is not a revision change; a reorder is refused instead when the set of siblings changed.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-018 and D-124 as one mechanism that later steps reuse: a column, a trigger, an argument and an error code.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rejected: A separate table of extra incomes: a second list and form with the same rules.
A one-off income among the monthly incomes: incomes are monthly and versioned (D-038).
decisions.title: An extra income is a transaction of its own kind
decisions.decision: Money coming in that is neither a salary nor a refund is a transaction of kind extra_income, with a date, an amount, an optional description and no category. It adds to the income total of the period containing its date (period_summaries.extra_income_total, included in income_total) and to nothing else. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults (the kind of record is the database developer's choice).
decisions.why: Answer to Q-052. One list, one form, one date rule and one paging contract for everything recorded by date; an import (step 6) produces credits and debits alike.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: A back-dated transaction may use an ended category
decisions.decision: A transaction goes on a category in force in the period containing its date. A back-dated transaction may therefore use a category that has since ended, when it was in force in that period; a category not yet in force then, or already ended then, is refused (category_not_in_force). list_categories_for_date gives the categories a date may use. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-053. Late receipts land where they belong (D-105) without reviving the category.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rejected: Dates up to the current period's end, refusing any boundary or terms change that would leave one outside (as briefed): see why.
Storing the period id on each transaction: it would have to be rewritten by every boundary operation.
decisions.title: Transactions are dated up to today
decisions.decision: A transaction is dated from the first period's start to today, and not after the last period's end (ended budgets). No period id is stored: a transaction belongs to the period containing its date and follows it through every boundary operation. With dates up to today no operation can leave a transaction outside every period (every operation keeps the current period's end on or after today, and the first period's start never moves); a deferred constraint checks it.
decisions.why: The brief allowed dates up to the current period's end. But a change of the primary income's terms re-projects that end (R-PERIOD-011) and could leave a future-dated transaction outside every period; refusing a pay-day change because of a future-dated receipt would couple unrelated actions. Transactions record what happened; planned charges are subscriptions (step 4).
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A merge voids or deletes rows one at a time (step 2 fix)
decisions.decision: private.rekey_period deletes each validity row that would never be in force after a merge on its own, and keeps it as a void row only when that delete fails on a foreign key. Step 2 tried one delete for all such rows and, if any was referenced, voided all of them, so an unreferenced income or category could linger as a void row.
decisions.why: Found while registering categories, whose subcategories and transactions reference them (D-091).

rejected: Hiding categories not in force: their spending would vanish from the rows but not from the result.
decisions.title: What the progress view counts
decisions.decision: A period's progress has one row per category and subcategory in force in it, and one for every category with transactions dated in it even when not in force then (an ended or void category, or one whose period changed through a boundary operation): expected 0, spending counted. Spending is expenses minus refunds and may be negative. Each expectation counts once per period whatever the period's length, like an income (R-INCOME-011). Totals are the sums of the rows, computed by the same functions (private.expectations_in_force, private.spending_between).
decisions.why: No transaction may drop out of the totals (the period result would lie), and the totals must never disagree with the rows.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Limits for categories and transactions
decisions.decision: Per budget at most 200 categories and subcategories in force and 2000 in all, and 200 000 transactions. Expectation amounts from 0 to 1 000 000 000 rappen as entered (per month or per year); transaction amounts from 1 to 1 000 000 000 rappen; descriptions at most 500 characters; a page of the transaction list at most 200 rows. Defined in one place in the step 3 migration.
decisions.why: Abuse bounds that no household reaches, and that keep every read bounded and every sum far inside bigint.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rejected: PostgREST offset paging (.range) on the view: unstable and slow deep in a long history.
decisions.title: The transaction list is paged by a cursor in an RPC
decisions.decision: list_transactions returns a page of at most 200 rows in the stable order (date desc, created_at desc, id desc); the next page passes the last row's date, created_at and id. Filters: dates, category (a group includes its subcategories), kind. Each page is an index range scan, however deep.
decisions.why: Offset paging slows down and shifts when rows are added; a keyset needs a unique order, and an RPC keeps the bound and the index use in the database.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Import sources: three PDF statements and the generic CSV import
decisions.decision: The import sources are the Migros Bank private-account statement, the Migros Bank credit-card bill (issued through Viseca and downloaded from its "one" app or portal) and the Yuh account statement, all as PDF files. Raiffeisen is dropped. TWINT needs no source of its own, because its entries appear in the Migros Bank account statement. The generic CSV import with column mapping stays. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-058. These are the statements the household receives; the product owner provided one sample of each, and none of them is a CSV export.
rejected: Presets for Raiffeisen and for a TWINT export (D-119): the household does not need Raiffeisen, and TWINT entries are already in the Migros Bank statement.
source: owner-request: product owner decision on the import sources, with sample statements, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Statements are parsed in the browser
decisions.decision: A statement is parsed in the browser; the PDF file never leaves the device. Only the extracted transactions are sent to the import function and saved. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: A statement holds much more personal data than its transactions (address, IBAN, balances, other people's names and phone numbers); a file that is never uploaded needs no protection on the server. The app has no server of its own, so parsing in the browser also needs no new backend.
rejected: Uploading the PDF to Supabase storage and parsing it on the server.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: An imported transaction is dated by its purchase date
decisions.decision: The date of an imported transaction is the purchase date when the statement gives one, otherwise the booking date. The value date is not used. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: The purchase date is when the money was spent, so the spending lands in the right period; booking dates lag one to four days behind and would move purchases made at the end of a period into the next one.
rejected: Always the booking date.
The value date.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Card-bill payments and own transfers are not expenses
decisions.decision: A payment of a credit-card bill and a transfer between the owner's own accounts are not expenses: the import flags them and skips them by default, and the user can import them anyway. The user's choice is remembered and proposed as the default the next time. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: The card's purchases are imported from the card bill itself, so importing its payment too would count them twice; a transfer to one's own account moves money without spending it.
rejected: Importing them like any other debit for the user to delete.
Dropping them without telling the user.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Salary credits are skipped, other credits are reviewed
decisions.decision: A salary credit that matches one of the budget's incomes is skipped, because that income already counts. Every other credit is proposed for review, either as a refund in a category or as extra income. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: Incomes are planned in the budget, so importing the salary as well would count it twice. Most other credits are refunds or shares of a bill paid back, not income.
rejected: Importing every credit as income.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Investment purchases are ordinary transactions
decisions.decision: A securities purchase, such as a savings-plan purchase on Yuh, is imported as an ordinary transaction for the user to categorise. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: The budget has no investment accounts yet; an ordinary transaction keeps the money visible and lets the user choose its category.
rejected: Skipping investment purchases.
Recording them as transfers to an investment account.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Interest and fee lines are imported
decisions.decision: Interest and fee lines of a statement, such as the late-payment interest of a card bill, are imported as transactions. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: They are money spent; leaving them out would hide real costs from the budget.
rejected: Skipping interest and fee lines.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A foreign-currency purchase counts in CHF, fees included
decisions.decision: For a purchase in a foreign currency, the amount is the CHF amount billed, fees included, and the original currency and amount are kept in the description. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: The CHF amount is what left the account (CHF is the only currency, R-MONEY-001); the original amount helps the user recognise the purchase.
rejected: The converted amount alone, with the fee as a separate transaction.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: French statements are supported first
decisions.decision: The statement parsers support the French versions of the three statements first; another language is added when a sample of it is available. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 as a default; the product owner may overrule it.
decisions.why: The samples are in French, and a parser can only be trusted once it is tested against a real layout.
rejected: Supporting German, Italian and English from the start, without samples.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The next salary is announced from the current period
decisions.decision: For the primary income the app announces the next salary as the day after the current period's end (nextSalary, src/features/periods/next-salary.ts), never income_overview.next_pay_date: the period's end already holds an early salary, a date set by hand and the projection. In the budget's last period the app announces the budget's end, and once the budget has ended nothing. Other incomes keep their own schedule's next pay date.
decisions.why: The step 2 browser review found the dashboard and the income card announcing the schedule (10.12) while the Periods page announced the period (11.01) for the salary that had just arrived early.
rejected: income_overview.next_pay_date for the primary income: it is the schedule's next pay date on or after today and knows nothing of boundaries.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Edit forms read their record by id and compare what they show
decisions.decision: Every edit form and removal confirmation reads its record by id (useRecord), independently of the list, filter or page it was opened from, and keeps the version it opened (useEditBase) whose revision it sends. The record's revision is its one revision source, but a form compares only the fields it shows: a newer revision that leaves them as they were becomes its base in silence (the user's own save in another form, another member changing another field). When a shown field changed: with nothing typed the form takes the other version and says what changed; with something typed it lists the other member's values field by field and offers "Load their version" or "Keep mine", which keeps only the fields the user edited (react-hook-form's dirty fields) so the save sends only those. A record deleted meanwhile is said to be gone. Built once (src/hooks/use-edit-base.ts, src/hooks/use-concurrent-form.ts, src/components/changed-elsewhere.tsx, src/features/budgets/record-queries.ts) and used by incomes, the budget's name and end date, categories and transactions; steps 4 to 7 reuse it.
decisions.why: The first version looked the record up in whatever list was loaded (a transaction moved to another period by another member read as a dead end), compared revisions only (saving one settings form flagged the other) and, after "Keep mine", sent every field, reverting the other member's untouched changes. D-124 asks to refuse the second save; reloading the form would lose what was typed, and silently retrying would overwrite the other member.
rejected: Looking the record up in the loaded list.
Comparing revisions only.
"Keep mine" sending every field of the form.
Reloading the form with the other version, discarding what was typed.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 3 screens review fixes, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Period progress lives on the dashboard
decisions.decision: The progress view of a period is one component on the dashboard, below the current period, showing the current period by default and any other through ?period=<id> with previous / next buttons. The Periods page links each period there, and each category row links to the transactions page filtered by that period and category. Every figure is the database's (period_summaries, get_period_progress); only the length of a row's bar is computed in the client, for display.
decisions.why: One implementation for the current and past periods (D-104), where people look first; the Periods page stays about boundaries.
rejected: A separate progress page per period: a second place showing the same figures.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16

rejected: Keeping the optional argument for one release (D-142): no release to stay compatible with.
decisions.title: Revisions are required; no direct writes
decisions.decision: Nothing is deployed, so every edit and removal RPC requires p_expected_revision (invalid_revision when missing), including step 2's set_budget_end_date, remove_income and set_primary_income (the budget's revision, since the primary income is a budget field). The direct renames of budgets and incomes are removed (no update privilege, no policy); renames go through rename_budget and update_income, which edits an income's name and terms in one call and returns its new revision (replacing rename_income and update_income_terms). Ordering categories stays outside the revision (D-142).
decisions.why: D-142 kept step 2's revision optional and the direct renames for a deployed release; there is none, and a check that a client may skip protects nothing. One income edit saves the two-call sequence that had to thread a revision between calls.

rejected: An idempotency key per request: it guards retries but not two members acting on what they each saw.
decisions.title: Boundary operations name the period they act on
decisions.decision: Periods have a revision. set_expected_pay_date, record_early_pay_date and reopen_previous_period take the current period's id and revision as the client read them (period_summaries.revision), and move_period_start the moved period's revision; each is refused with record_changed when that period is no longer current, changed or is gone. A write paired with a preview (update_income, set_primary_income) can send p_previewed_end_date and is refused when the current period would end on another day than the preview showed.
decisions.why: A reopen called twice, by two members or by a retry after a timeout, merged two periods and lost the merged period's own records (review finding 1).

rejected: Dropping the mark for past periods: it still says the boundary differs from the schedule.
decisions.title: A boundary on the schedule's day is not set by hand
decisions.decision: move_period_start marks the previous period's end as set by hand only when the boundary is not where the schedule puts it (the previous period's projected end, the day before); moving it back clears the mark. Without a date, move_period_start moves the boundary to the schedule. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-071: moving a boundary and moving it back left both periods marked as set by hand, and nothing could clear the mark on a past period.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision on the step 3 database review, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: Limits (revised); costs depend on the budget's own rows
decisions.decision: Per budget at most 200 categories and subcategories in force and 500 in all, void rows not counted, and 50 000 transactions; amounts, descriptions and pages as in D-148. Every read and write costs what the budget holds: no query scans another budget's rows (lookups by category are planned for the actual id), and each deferred check of a row checks that row, so a merge or a move to "Other" at the limits stays within a few seconds (the hosted statement timeout is 8 s).
decisions.why: D-148's bounds were far beyond a household and a free-tier database; the categories page scanned every budget's transactions, and a reopen with 2000 categories took 13 s because each row's check scanned the whole budget (review findings 4 and limits).

rejected: Recreating the category under the same name: two histories for one thing.
decisions.title: Count from an earlier period, and restore
decisions.decision: Two explicit corrections, like the others: extend_category makes a category count from an earlier period (its earliest expectation there unless an amount is given; a subcategory never before its group), and restore_category restores an ended category from the current period, expecting nothing in the periods between its end and now so that their totals do not change, or, as a correction, from the period it ended, as if it had never ended (a subcategory needs its group in force). Both keep the group and subcategory shape and are reported by preview_reopen like any other recorded change. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-082 and review finding 5: a category could not be made to count before its first period, so older transactions (and later the import of older statements) were refused, and an ended category with transactions could neither be restored nor recreated.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision on the step 3 database review, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: The registry checks what it promises
decisions.decision: private.check_period_keyed_table also refuses a validity table whose check constraints on first_seq and end_seq alone refuse a void row (each is evaluated for first_seq = end_seq = 1), and a version table with no foreign key from its entity column to its entity table.
decisions.why: D-091 and the docs said both were checked; the step 2 check accepted either (review).

decisions.title: Client types show what can be null
decisions.decision: get_period_progress and list_categories_for_date return named row types (public.category_progress_row, public.category_choice), so the generated types mark their fields as nullable; reorder_categories takes p_parent_id last, optional (null: the top level). docs/database.md says which fields are actually never null.
decisions.why: The generated types claimed amount, cadence and parent_id were never null and required a parent id for the top level (review finding 6).

decisions.title: Previews take the write's arguments
decisions.decision: preview_expected_pay_date is replaced by preview_update_income (the income and the terms and correction period update_income takes) and preview_set_primary_income (the income), computed with the write's own helpers (private.income_edit_seq, private.income_new_terms, private.reprojected_end), including a correction shadowed by a later version.
decisions.why: The old preview could not express a correction from an earlier period, and previewed a shadowed correction wrongly (review).

decisions.title: Corrections work in an ended budget
decisions.decision: An explicit correction names its period and works in an ended budget: create_category with p_from_period_id is accepted there like update_category, end_category, extend_category and add_transaction; only what applies from the current period answers budget_ended.
decisions.why: create_category refused a correction that the other category RPCs accepted (review).

decisions.title: A transaction keeps its category in its period
decisions.decision: A transaction may always keep the category it already has while it stays in the same period; the in-force check applies only when the category or the period changes. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16.
decisions.why: A transaction whose category had ended, or had been voided by a reopen, could not be edited at all (review finding 3).
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision on the step 3 database review, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: Values that only mean something together are one field for concurrent edits
decisions.decision: A view of a record's fields (FieldView in src/hooks/use-edit-base.ts) can name several form fields as one group: a category's amount and cadence, an income's pay day and weekend rule (step 4: a subscription's price and cadence). The group is one field everywhere a concurrent edit looks: detection and the banner compare and show it as one value; "Keep mine" keeps the whole group as the form shows it when the user edited any part of it, and takes the other member's version whole when they edited none; and the save sends the whole group when any part differs. This amends D-136's "keeps only the fields the user edited" for groups.
decisions.why: Keeping dirty fields one by one combined two members' edits into a value neither chose: with 200.00 per month, Sam set 50.00 per month while Ann switched the cadence to per year, and "Keep mine" sent only the cadence, storing 50.00 per year, which neither chose; Ann's form showed 200.00 per year, which is what is now kept.
rejected: Keeping each dirty form field on its own (D-136 as first built).
Treating the whole record as one field: an untouched name would revert the other member's rename.

decisions.title: Editing a subscription's schedule sets its next charge
decisions.decision: A subscription's terms carry the date its schedule counts from. An edit from now that gives a next charge date (after today) makes it the next charge, the later ones following at the cadence; a new cadence without a date continues from the next charge date of the current schedule; any other edit keeps the schedule. A charge already created never moves and a date already passed is never charged. A correction from an earlier period may name any date: it changes the terms recorded for those periods and the charges still to come, never those already created. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16 (step 4 brief: decide what an edit to the schedule does to the next charge date).
decisions.why: The user thinks of a schedule change as "the next charge is then"; anchoring the new schedule on that date cannot move or duplicate a charge already made.
rejected: Recomputing the whole schedule from the first charge date under the new cadence, which could skip or repeat a charge around the change.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision for step 4, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: Charges are created by the catch-up, exactly once per date
decisions.decision: There is no server, so subscription charges are created by the same catch-up that creates periods: whenever a member opens the budget and before every write, every charge date up to the database's today that has not been materialised is created, exactly once per subscription and date however many members or tabs trigger it at once (under the budget lock). Missed dates are caught up. Each subscription keeps a watermark (charged_through) that only moves forward, so a charge that was deleted or answered as not gone through is never created again for that date, and no edit, correction or reopen creates a charge for a date already passed. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-054. A watermark rather than one tombstone per dismissed charge: the same guarantee, with nothing to keep for dismissed dates.
rejected: A scheduled job: there is no server (D-003).
Recreating a dismissed charge on the next catch-up.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision for step 4, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: Interest at period creation; the projection and "never"
decisions.decision: Interest is applied when a new period is created, on the balance at that moment, as one twelfth of the yearly rate rounded half up to the rappen, as an entry of that period in the debt's history (dated at the period's start). It is applied exactly once per debt and period however the period came to exist (roll-over, catch-up over several periods, an early salary), and a reopen that merges a period removes the interest entry that period created. No interest on a balance of zero or less. A planned payment less than or equal to one period's interest means the debt never ends. The projection has a horizon of 600 periods (50 years) beyond which it answers "never". Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to Q-055. Periods run salary to salary, so the period, not the calendar month, is the step of interest; tying the entry to its period keeps a reopen exact.
rejected: Interest at the end of a period, after its payments: the end of the current period is not a fact until the next one starts.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision for step 4, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: A non-monthly subscription's monthly cost
decisions.decision: The monthly cost of a subscription, for the committed figure, is its price divided by the number of months in its cadence (1, 3, 6, 12), rounded half up to the rappen; totals add the rounded monthly costs (as D-140). The charge itself counts in full in the period containing its date. Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: Answer to the subscription part of Q-050, the same rule as yearly expectations (D-140).
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision for step 4, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: Subscriptions and debts are versioned like incomes; ending follows the established rule
decisions.decision: A subscription's terms (price, cadence, category, schedule) and a debt's terms (interest rate, planned monthly payment) are versioned like incomes and category amounts, through the registry (private.period_keyed_tables), so committed figures and projections for past periods use the terms in force then, and a reopen treats them like any other recorded change. Ending or deleting follows the established rule: something that has counted in the past is ended from now and kept in the past; something that never counted is deleted. A debt with linked payments, or a subscription with charges, is never silently destroyed (a reopen keeps it as a void row). Decided by the project coordinator on 2026-11-16, on the product owner's instruction to proceed on the coordinator's defaults.
decisions.why: One mechanism for every versioned record; the user's history is never lost to a removal or a reopen.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision for step 4, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

decisions.title: A charge is a transaction with its scheduled date and a review state
decisions.decision: An automatic charge is an ordinary expense transaction linked to its subscription, with the scheduled date it was created for (charge_date, unique per subscription; the transaction's own date may be edited) and review_state 'awaiting_confirmation' until a member confirms it (confirm_subscription_charge). "Did not go through" (dismiss_subscription_charge) deletes it; delete_transaction does the same. Editing a charge keeps it a charge and does not confirm it. The column review_state is the one step 6 planned for imports (D-118), which adds its own value.
decisions.why: A charge must count in totals at once (D-109) and be edited like any transaction (R-SUBSCRIPTION-074): it is one. A single review state serves both automatic charges and, later, imports.
rejected: A separate table of charges pointing at transactions: two records for one fact.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A subscription counts from its first period
decisions.decision: A subscription is in force from the period it is created in (or, as an explicit correction, from an earlier one); its charges are the scheduled dates on or after its first charge date in the periods where it is in force, so creating it creates at once, awaiting confirmation, the charges of its first period up to today (for a back-dated one, those of the earlier periods too). Dates before its first period are never charged. When the budget is at its transaction limit, charges wait (the watermark stops before the first that does not fit) and are created once there is room.
decisions.why: A first charge date in the past sets the schedule without flooding closed periods with charges the user may have recorded by hand; an explicit correction is the only way to add charges to closed periods. Waiting at the limit never loses a charge.
rejected: Charging every date since the first charge date, back to the budget's start.
Skipping charges that do not fit the limit.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Links: payments are expenses in the debt's category
decisions.decision: A transaction is linked through add_transaction (p_debt_id or p_subscription_id) or link_transaction (which also unlinks; unlinking a charge makes it an ordinary confirmed transaction). update_transaction keeps the link. A linked transaction is an expense; a debt payment is in the debt's category; the debt or subscription is in force in the period of the date; a linked transaction keeping its period and category keeps its link even when the debt's category changed or it ended (as D-159). A refund is never a payment.
decisions.why: Step 3 callers of update_transaction send every field; a link they do not know of must not be dropped. Payments in the debt's category keep the category's spending and the debt's payments the same money.
rejected: Refunds linked to a debt as reversed payments.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Debt principal, balance adjustments and corrections
decisions.decision: A debt's principal can change only while it has no payment, interest or adjustment (a typo at creation); afterwards the balance is adjusted. adjust_debt_balance takes the balance the bank shows and the database stores the difference as a dated entry (no entry when there is none), so a payment recorded meanwhile cannot make it wrong; an adjustment can be deleted. A correction of a debt's terms from an earlier period records the terms for those periods and the projection, and never recomputes interest already added (each entry records the rate and balance it used); a wrong past interest is fixed with an adjustment. Ending a debt keeps its remaining amount. A debt created from an earlier period (a correction) starts its history at that period's start and gets no interest for periods that already existed.
decisions.why: Interest entries are facts of the moment a period was created; recomputing them could not reproduce that moment.
rejected: Recomputing every later interest entry after a rate correction.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Categories in use by subscriptions and debts
decisions.decision: end_category refuses (category_in_use) a category that a subscription or debt in force from that period still uses; one that any subscription version or debt references is ended rather than deleted, like one with transactions. Adding the first subcategory to a category with subscriptions or debts needs "Other", and moves them there with its transactions and expectations (create_category redefined). category_overview gains in_use and accounts for the references in removal_deletes.
decisions.why: Otherwise a removal would fail on a foreign key, a charge would land on a category not in force or on a group, or a debt's payments would have nowhere to go.
rejected: Ending the subscriptions and debts with the category.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Limits for subscriptions and debts
decisions.decision: Per budget at most 50 subscriptions in force and 200 in all, 50 debts in force and 200 in all (void rows not counted), and 5000 balance adjustments; prices, principals and planned payments up to 1 000 000 000 rappen; interest rates 0 to 100 % with three decimals; a schedule date at most ten years ahead; a debt's balance never grows beyond 1 000 000 000 000 rappen through interest or an adjustment. Automatic charges count towards the 50 000 transactions (D-153). Defined in one place in the step 4 migration.
decisions.why: Abuse bounds: with 50 monthly subscriptions, ten years of absence create 6000 charges in one catch-up, within the hosted statement timeout.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The payoff projection
decisions.decision: debt_overview projects, for a debt in force in a budget with a current period: 'paid_off' when nothing remains; otherwise the planned payment still due in the current period (the planned payment minus what was paid in it) is paid first, then each later period adds its interest and receives the planned payment, until nothing remains ('ends', with payments_left and expected_end_date, the projected end of the period of the last payment, future periods following the primary income's schedule) or the planned payment does not exceed a period's interest or the horizon is reached ('never').
decisions.why: Counting this period's payment once, whether or not it was made yet, keeps the end date stable through the period.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Charts: shadcn chart (Recharts), theme colours, lazy route
decisions.decision: Charts use shadcn's chart component on Recharts. Series colours are the theme tokens --chart-1 to --chart-5, set for light and dark to the palette of D-405 (every pair validated for colour-vision deficiencies, each at least 3:1 on the card); identity is never colour alone (lines have their own mark and dash, there is a legend and a table). The page that draws a chart is its own lazily loaded route, so Recharts never reaches the first load. A debt's chart is a step line of the balance on a time axis (dates spaced by days, no time zone), its value axis scaled to the balances so a few payments show (zero drawn when in range).
decisions.why: Step 5 needs more charts; shadcn's component fits the existing UI kit; the production Content-Security-Policy allows the inline style element it writes (style-src 'unsafe-inline') and no script.
rejected: A hand-drawn SVG chart (no library): step 5 would redo it.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, independent review of the step 4 and step 5 screens at a24615e, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The client adds up no debt amounts
decisions.decision: The debts page shows what is still owed in all, and how many debts owe it, as debt_totals gives them (D-216); each debt's paid share and overpaid amount are paid_percent and overpaid_by. Nothing about a debt is added up or computed in the client. (Until the database gave the total, the page added up the remaining amounts of the debts in force.)
decisions.why: C-LOGIC-003: the database owns the figures; Q-110 asked for the total and D-216 answered it. Reworded rather than superseded: the migration that gives the total names this decision.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 2, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A debt has its own page
decisions.decision: Each debt opens on its own route (/debts/<id>), with its figures, chart, history and actions; an unknown or deleted id says the debt does not exist. A payment in the history leads to the transactions of its period (there is no page for one transaction).
decisions.why: The chart and the history need room, and the route can be loaded lazily (D-190).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: What the subscription form previews
decisions.decision: The form asks the database for the dates (subscription_charge_dates) of the schedule it describes: a new subscription from its first charge date, starting at the period it counts from, the dates up to today flagged as charged at once; an edit with a new next charge date from that date; a new cadence alone, from now, from the current next charge date; otherwise the current schedule from its next charge. The next charge date of an edit is optional (blank keeps the schedule) and, from now, must be after today.
decisions.why: D-170 decides what an edit does to the schedule; the form must show it before saving without computing a schedule itself (C-LOGIC-003).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Changing a transaction's debt link takes several calls
decisions.decision: update_transaction never changes a link (D-177), so an edit that changes the debt a transaction pays calls link_transaction to remove the old link before the fields change, update_transaction, then link_transaction to add the new one, each with the revision the previous call returned. They are not one transaction: a failure part-way leaves the steps already done (the form shows the error, the lists are read again).
decisions.why: Removing first and linking last keeps every intermediate state valid (a payment is always in its debt's category). Q-111 asks for one call.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Answering an automatic charge
decisions.decision: A charge awaiting confirmation is answered from the dashboard card or from the transactions list. "It went through" confirms at once; "It did not go through" asks first and says the charge will not be created again for that date. When another member answered first (record_changed, or the charge is gone), the list is read again and a message says so; nothing is resent.
decisions.why: Dismissing deletes a transaction for good (R-SUBSCRIPTION-077); confirming is harmless.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A subscription's terms are one group for concurrent edits
decisions.decision: Applying D-160 to subscriptions: price, cadence and the new next charge date of the edit form are one group (a new cadence moves the schedule, so the date belongs with it). A debt's rate and planned payment stay independent fields.
decisions.why: A price kept from one member and a cadence from another would charge an amount nobody chose (the step 3 category case).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A correction starts from the terms of its period
decisions.decision: The correction forms (incomes, categories, subscriptions, debts) read the terms in force in the period chosen from the version tables the contract makes readable (income_versions, category_expectations, subscription_versions, debt_versions: the row with the greatest effective_from_seq not after the period's seq), show them as the starting values, and send only what the user changes from them. Until the database gives these terms itself (Q-130), this lookup is the client's one use of the version tables.
decisions.why: Sending today's terms with every correction wrote them over the past: a category changed alone took the price from 19.90 to 24.90 in period 1.
rejected: Showing today's terms and sending only changed fields: the user cannot see what they are correcting.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 1, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: An overpaid debt is paid off; the total counts what is still owed
decisions.decision: A debt whose remaining amount is negative is shown as "Paid off · overpaid by CHF x", its figure labelled "Overpaid", never "Remaining CHF -x". The total across debts counts only debts that still owe something (overpaid and paid-off ones add nothing and are not counted in "N debts"); the database will give it (round 2).
decisions.why: Decided by the coordinator after the review: a negative "remaining" reads as an error.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 1, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A charge is named by its own date
decisions.decision: An automatic charge is named to the user by the date of its transaction, the date the lists show; when a member moved it, the date it was scheduled for is added ("scheduled for"), and the dismissal says the charge will not be created again for its scheduled date.
decisions.why: The row, the button names and the removal dialog showed two different dates for one charge.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 1, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The debt chart: one point per date, round ticks, few marks
decisions.decision: The chart draws one point per date (the balance after its last event) on to today; its tooltip lists every event of the date with its amount and resulting balance. Value ticks are round (1, 2, 2.5 or 5 times a power of ten rappen, with rappen shown when needed); time ticks fall on month or year starts beyond three months. Beyond 24 dates only balance adjustments are marked (interest comes every period and would bury the line); the opening is a hollow square, a payment a dot. The history table shows the latest 12 events until all are asked for. A debt with only its opening shows a sentence instead. The chart is one named image, not a keyboard stop; the table is its text.
decisions.why: The review found repeated labels, buried lines and same-day events hidden behind one another.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 1, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Ending from an earlier period says both outcomes
decisions.decision: Whether a removal deletes is known beforehand only for a removal from now (removal_deletes). Ending a subscription or a debt from an earlier period is therefore offered as "End or delete", saying when each happens, until the database answers for a chosen period (Q-131).
decisions.why: The dialog said "End" and the database deleted.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 1, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A subscription's nominal day is kept apart from its anchor
decisions.decision: Each version of a subscription's terms stores its nominal day of the month (charge_day, 1 to 31) beside the anchor date: the day of the first charge date, or of a next charge date given with a change. Charge dates fall on that day, clamped to each month's length. A change of cadence without a date re-anchors on the next charge of the current schedule and keeps the nominal day.
decisions.why: A schedule re-anchored on a clamped date (28 February) otherwise drifts to the 28th for good.
rejected: Deriving the day from the anchor date: a clamped anchor loses the day (the review's S2 finding).
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Catch-up in bounded steps, no runaway error
decisions.decision: A read's catch-up (ensure_periods, get_current_period, the charge list, the previews) creates at most 120 periods per call with their interest and charges and keeps them; my_budgets.caught_up says whether more remains and the client calls ensure_periods until it returns 0. A write catches up in full first. Step 2's period_generation_runaway error is gone: the loop is bounded by the dates, so opening a budget always succeeds and progresses after any absence.
decisions.why: Review finding M2: after about 13 years of absence a budget could never be opened again.
rejected: Raising the runaway limit: still a cliff, only further away.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A debt's opened date bounds its history
decisions.decision: A debt has an opened date (opened_on): today for a debt recorded from now, its first period's start for one recorded from an earlier period. Payments and balance adjustments dated before it are refused with before_debt_opened.
decisions.why: The principal is the balance on the opened date; an entry before it would count twice or not at all.
rejected: Moving opened_on back to the earliest entry: the principal would no longer be the balance on that date.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Future period ends follow the catch-up
decisions.decision: The debt projection takes the end of the k-th future period from the catch-up's own projected end: the next period starts the day after the current one ends, whatever its end (set by hand early or late), and later ones follow the pay schedule in force.
decisions.why: Review finding M1: a closed form from the current period's start was wrong when its end had been set early.
rejected: A separate closed form from the current period: a second implementation (C-LOGIC-001).
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A charge is pending when its date is due
decisions.decision: Each subscription keeps the first scheduled date not yet charged (next_due). The fast path of every read checks it without the lock; only a due date with room in the budget makes a read take the lock and write. The bookkeeping columns (charged_through, next_due) change neither the revision nor updated_at.
decisions.why: Review finding S4: a read crossing a day with no charge due took the lock and touched every subscription row.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Moving the period end through an income edit needs its preview
decisions.decision: update_income on the primary income takes p_previewed_end_date; when the edit would move the current period's end, a missing or different value is refused with preview_required.
decisions.why: A step 3 leftover from the review: the end of the current period moved without the member having seen it.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A balance adjustment without a date
decisions.decision: adjust_debt_balance without a date dates the adjustment at the charge horizon: today, or the budget's last day once the budget has ended.
decisions.why: An ended budget has no today in it; its last day is the latest date an entry can have.
rejected: Refusing an adjustment without a date in an ended budget.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A debt's category is part of its terms
decisions.decision: The category moves from the debt to its versions (debt_versions.category_id): a change of category from a period on keeps the payments of earlier periods in the category they were in, and the coverage rule (R-CATEGORY-130) is checked per version like a subscription's.
decisions.why: Review finding S1: a debt's category changed for all periods at once, leaving earlier payments in another category than their debt.
rejected: Keeping one category per debt and refusing a change once paid.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Reopen re-keys referrers before categories and trims versions at an end
