decisions.title: How entries become import rows
decisions.decision: toImportBatch(statement) returns the source (migros_account, migros_card, yuh), the statement's dates (its period; for a card bill the day after the previous bill to the bill date), the rows in statement order each with its entry number beside it, the entries not sent with a code, and the adjustments made. A row has date, amount, direction, description (cut to 500 characters at a code-point boundary), merchant (200), bank_transaction_id (dropped, not cut, above 100), hint and details. Details: purchase_time, booking_date, value_date, card, original_currency with original_amount in that currency's minor unit, exchange_rate as the printed decimal string, fee in rappen, merchant_category, security (the ISIN), location (place and country code); above 2000 bytes they are dropped in this order: location, security, merchant_category, exchange_rate, original amount and currency together, fee, card, value_date, purchase_time, booking_date. An own transfer goes without description and merchant (its payee is the holder). transfer_to_person is given to a TWINT payment to a phone number only: the statements do not show whether the payee of a payment or standing order is a person.
decisions.why: The import function refuses a row with any other key or out of its bounds; shortening in a stated way and saying so keeps the import going and visible. Integers and decimal strings keep money exact.
rejected: Refusing a statement with a field too long.
Truncating ids.
Guessing persons from payee names.

decisions.title: Entries of 0.00 are shown, not imported
decisions.decision: An entry of 0.00 (a currency conversion rounded to nothing) stays in the entry list with the handling nothing-to-import, and the mapping lists it among the entries not sent, with the code zero-amount.
decisions.why: The import function refuses an amount of 0, and leaving the line out of the list would make the statement look incomplete next to the PDF.

decisions.title: Chart palette re-derived: all pairs apart under every colour-vision deficiency
decisions.decision: The five chart tokens are, light: #3c5296, #d06002, #0da3a8, #a668f9, #812f52 (each at least 3:1 on the white card); dark: #2265db, #df692a, #14a185, #a77fd4, #a9348d (at least 3:1 on the dark card). Chosen by a search in OKLCH and checked over all pairs (not only neighbours) by two measures: the dataviz validator (OKLab: light worst 12.0 protan/deutan, 14.4 tritan, normal vision 16.4; dark 11.0 and 9.9, normal vision 17.4; target 8, normal-vision floor 15) and the reviewer's (Machado 2009 simulation, CIE76: every pair at least 29.5 light and 22.8 dark under protan, deutan and tritan; floor 20). Lines also carry their slot's mark and dash. D-190's claim that "marks have shapes" was not true of the category chart before this change, and the earlier light tokens were 2.2 to 4.4:1 on the card; D-190 is corrected to point here.
decisions.why: Five lines can all cross, so every pair must stay apart, under deuteranopia, protanopia and tritanopia, in both themes; the debt chart uses the same tokens and keeps passing.

decisions.title: One request id per add, from the form
decisions.decision: Every add form (transaction, category, income, subscription, debt) generates one request id when it opens and sends it as p_client_id with every save; it gets a new one after a save went through (the transaction form's "save and add another" included) and after request_reused, and keeps it after a lost answer or any other refusal, so the same save sent again records once. A refusal changes nothing in the database, so keeping the id after one is safe: a corrected save with the same id is a first use. The lost-answer message now says that saving again is safe; request_reused says the values were already saved with other content and to check the list before saving again.

rejected: A new id per click (a retry after a lost answer would record twice).

decisions.title: The comparison screens take what the database now gives
decisions.decision: Side by side opens on the database's default (the last two completed periods) and says in words, under the picker, in the column heading and in the period list, which chosen side is still running (a_is_current, b_is_current). The categories view shows active_average_spent ("over the N periods it was in use") under the average where active_count differs from completed_count, and both views take "over the plan" from the database's flags. decisions.title: The import page: read here, previewed under the import's own batch, sent in parts
decisions.decision: A PDF is read with readStatementFile (pdf.js and the parsers load on the first file, in chunks of their own) and mapped with toImportBatch; a CSV is mapped on the page. The client generates the batch id when the rows are ready and names it in every preview and every part. A member's choice is sent only where it differs from what the database proposes (a row's action, a credit's kind, a category in force on its date), so choices are remembered only where the member made one. The preview is asked per part of 500 rows, again 400 ms after the last change; the import is offered only once every part's answer is current, then sends the same rows. The rows are drawn 100 at a time with a filter (all, to import, skipped, invalid); the statement's extra data is in a disclosure per row. After the import: the counts from the answers, the rows not imported (list_import_skipped_rows) with "import anyway", the link to the review and undo.
decisions.why: R-IMPORT-252 and R-IMPORT-208 ask the preview to equal the write; the page must stay usable with 1200 rows on a phone.
rejected: Sending every choice explicitly (it would remember choices the member never made).
One preview call for all rows (the function takes 500).

decisions.title: An interrupted import is resumed by opening the same file
decisions.decision: While parts are sent the page asks before leaving. The batch id, the parts confirmed, the source and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the rows are kept in localStorage (never the rows: they hold bank data); after a reload the page says an import stopped after part n of m. Opening the same statement again (same fingerprint) reuses the batch id: every part is sent again and those already recorded answer as before. A finished import removes the note; "forget it" removes it by hand.
decisions.why: The rows must not be stored on the device; the import is idempotent by batch and part, so sending all parts again is safe.
rejected: Keeping the rows to resume without the file (bank data in browser storage).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The CSV mapping
decisions.decision: The separator is detected among semicolon, comma and tab (the one that splits the first lines into equal numbers of cells, the most cells winning) and can be changed; a file that is not UTF-8 is read as Windows-1252. The header's names pre-fill the mapping for the user to check. A date format fills itself only when it alone reads every date; otherwise the user chooses among DD.MM.YYYY, DD.MM.YY, MM.DD.YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD and DD-MM-YYYY. Amounts: one signed column (the user says what a negative is) or money out and money in; a decimal point or comma; apostrophes, spaces or the other mark as thousands separators; a trailing minus or brackets; more than two non-zero decimals is refused, never rounded. The statement dates sent are the earliest and latest row dates. The mapping is remembered per budget and header in localStorage.
decisions.why: R-IMPORT-082; Swiss exports use semicolons, decimal commas and DD.MM.YYYY, and 03.04 is ambiguous.
rejected: Guessing day-first for ambiguous dates.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 screens (part B, import), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The review in the transactions list
decisions.decision: A "to review" filter (review=1) and an import's filter (batch=<id>) are chips kept in the address; each imported row shows "to review" or "needs a category", a confirm button (none, with why, while in "to categorise") and the statement's data in a disclosure. Confirm all applies to the batch when one is filtered. After an edit gives an imported transaction to review a real category, the page offers "always put this merchant in this category?" with the merchant key the database computed and the number of others waiting in "to categorise" whose key contains it (read from list_transactions, up to 200); not offered when a rule's fragment is already contained in the key. decisions.title: An import token's secret stays in its dialog
decisions.decision: The token dialog calls create_import_token itself, outside the query library (D-472), and keeps the secret in its own state only, set to null when it closes; no query or mutation holds it or a closure that reaches it, so once the dialog is closed and garbage collected nothing reaches the secret (checked with a heap snapshot). The dialog says it is shown once, offers a copy button, and says to put it in the environment of the session that runs the script as BUDGET_IMPORT_TOKEN, never in a conversation (docs/import-script.md).

decisions.title: "To categorise" in the screens
decisions.decision: Pickers (transaction, subscription, debt, rule) drop the categories flagged is_to_categorise from list_categories_for_date / category_overview. The budget page lists it with a mark ("Import"), "No plan", what it is for, and an edit form that changes the name only; "add a subcategory" is not offered and "remove" is disabled with the reason while it holds transactions. decisions.title: Page strings load with the pages
decisions.decision: The strings of the import (step 6), the comparison (step 5) and the subscriptions, debts, charges and corrections (step 4) are three chunks (src/locales/groups), loaded with the budget pages by their lazy routes, which wait for them before rendering, so no key shows while they load. decisions.title: Migrations before the first deployment
decisions.decision: No database has been deployed yet. Until the first deployment, any migration file may be corrected in place, whichever step it belongs to; the first deployment freezes every migration file then present, and from then on every change is a new migration.
decisions.why: Fix rounds of a step under review would otherwise stack migrations that only repair code nobody has run, and the reviewed file would no longer be the one that runs.
rejected: A new migration for every fix from the start: the reviewed code and the code that runs drift apart before anything is deployed.

decisions.title: What a token learns of the room
decisions.decision: A token call is refused with transaction_limit_reached whenever the budget has room for fewer transactions than a token call's maximum rows (250), whatever rows it sends and before any planning: a token learns one bit ("nearly full"), never the count. A signed-in member keeps the exact answer (detail {"fits": n}).
decisions.why: Counting only the rows sent let a token learn the exact room below 500 by sending 1, 2, 3 rows that can never be imported (the re-review's should-fix 1).
rejected: Refusing only when the rows sent do not fit: an exact oracle of the room.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Import storage per budget is bounded
decisions.decision: Whatever members and tokens do, a budget's import storage is bounded. Within a rolling 24 hours (members and tokens together): 20 000 rows submitted to a write and 50 new batches (import_limit_reached), 20 tokens created, deleted ones included (token_limit_reached). Kept: 2 000 batches (at the limit, the oldest batches that hold no transaction and no skipped row any more go first; import_limit_reached when none can), the newest 20 000 skipped rows (older ones go; the batch's counts stay), the newest 50 chunk answers and none older than 7 days (a chunk whose answer is forgotten stays recorded, so sending it again answers chunk_expired and never imports it twice), and staged preview parts for a day, at most 100. Measured with incompressible text at every limit: a skipped row takes about 3 kB and a 500-row chunk answer about 380 kB, so a day adds at most about 85 MB and all that is kept beyond the transactions is at most about 110 MB (skipped rows 66 MB, chunk answers 19 MB, staged parts 11 MB, recorded chunks and batches about 15 MB).
decisions.why: The re-review stored 39 MB in 7 s through chunks and recycled 30 tokens in 4.4 s: each call was bounded, nothing bounded the total.
rejected: Refusing at the kept limits only: a stolen token could block imports for good.
Only a time-based pruning: no total bound.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Token calls never queue
decisions.decision: A token call never waits for another token call: another call of the same token doing work answers token_busy at once, and when the two slots for token work (all budgets together) are taken the call answers imports_busy at once; neither does any work or counts, and the script waits and sends again. A working call waits at most a second for its budget's lock (budget_busy, counted) and takes at most 250 rows (a member's call 500); with the merchant key's bounded steps and the duplicate lookup by index its database time stays far within the anon statement timeout (measured worst case about 0.3 s on a 45 000-transaction budget). Were it cancelled all the same, it answers call_cancelled and still counts. A visitor with only the publishable key can still make PostgREST read and parse a request body of any size the gateway lets through (Q-280) and receive invalid_token; every other function is refused.
decisions.why: A cancelled transaction cannot be counted, and calls of one token waiting on its lock piled up until the API stalled for every budget (re-review M-2).
rejected: Counting in a separate committed transaction (dblink): an extension and a connection per call for what bounded work and try-locks already give.
Keeping 500 rows a token call: under a 40-loop hammer on a loaded machine one call in 170 hit the statement timeout.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The cleaner keeps joiners where text needs them (revises D-376)
decisions.decision: A zero-width joiner or non-joiner stays between two characters that are not white space (an emoji sequence, Persian or Indic text) and goes elsewhere; interlinear annotation marks (U+FFF9 to U+FFFB) and the language tag (U+E0001) go; a text left with nothing visible (only Hangul fillers, blank braille patterns, joiners, variation selectors or tag characters) is empty, so a name made only of them is refused (invalid_name). Tag characters after a flag stay.
decisions.why: Removing every joiner broke emoji families and Persian words, while names made of invisible fillers passed as non-empty (re-review, cleaner).
rejected: Removing the fillers everywhere: some are real characters of Hangul or braille text.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A statement previewed in parts (answers Q-270 and Q-274)
decisions.decision: preview_import_part(p_budget_id, p_batch_id, p_part, p_rows) previews part p_part of a statement before any part is written: it takes into account what the batch's parts before it absorb (duplicates, matches) and the choices they send, as well as the chunks already written, so for a statement up to 100 parts of 500 rows its counts and per-row answers equal what import_transactions then does with the same parts in the same order, absent changes by others. It answers one object: rows (as preview_import), part and statement totals (rows and each action; the rows to import by kind, count and amount), the parts covered, the room and whether the statement fits. Previewing a part again forgets the staged parts from it on. preview_import keeps its shape.
decisions.why: The screens compared the write with a per-part preview that could not know what earlier parts absorb; the summary had no amounts because the client never adds them (C-LOGIC-003).
rejected: Previewing the whole statement in one call: answers beyond 1000 rows.
Changing preview_import's answer: the screens read its rows.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Remembered choices are the member's own (answers Q-276; revises D-314)
decisions.decision: Only a choice the member sent with a row (action import or skip, or "import anyway") is remembered; a default the import applied is not. A row's choice_key is the key its choice is remembered under: its merchant key, or own_transfer for an own transfer without description and merchant (no merchant key can contain "_"), so an own transfer's choice is remembered too.
decisions.why: The contract called them a member's choices while the import stored every default, and an own transfer without a description had no key at all.
rejected: A key per account for own transfers: the row carries no account.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A rule's preview (answers Q-271)
decisions.decision: preview_merchant_rule(p_budget_id, p_fragment, p_category_id) answers, without writing, the fragment as it would be stored, the existing rule that already covers it (the one the import picks: the longest fragment it contains), whether a rule with that fragment exists, and how many transactions waiting in "to categorise" the rule would move to that category (one implementation with the rule's apply).
decisions.why: The screens repeated the "contains" test in the client over at most 200 transactions (C-LOGIC-003).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Forget a remembered choice (answers Q-272)
decisions.decision: forget_import_choice(p_budget_id, p_flag, p_counterparty_key) deletes a remembered choice; the next import of that entry applies the default again. It answers whether one was forgotten.
decisions.why: A member could only override a choice at the next import.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: One batch by its id (answers Q-275)
decisions.decision: get_import_batch(p_batch_id) answers the batch as list_import_batches gives it, to members of its budget (import_batch_not_found otherwise).
decisions.why: A summary or a link to one batch had to scan pages.
rejected: A p_batch_id argument on list_import_batches: another overload of a paged call.

decisions.title: Editing in "to categorise" (answers Q-273)
decisions.decision: An imported transaction waiting in "to categorise" can be edited (amount, date, description, links) while it keeps that category; update_transaction refuses only moving a transaction into it, and confirming it there.
decisions.why: The guard already allowed it; the contract did not say so.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Client request ids answer members only (revises D-390)
decisions.decision: A call with p_client_id checks membership first: before the id is looked at, before the catch-up gate and before the budget lock (and again under the lock). A signed-in outsider or a removed member gets budget_not_found for every budget and every client id; a replay answers a current member only rows of the budget it names; add_income replayed after the income was removed answers no income, like the other calls.
decisions.why: A removed member replaying a client id read the budget's current rows for 7 days, and an outsider learned request_reused and catching_up (re-review M-1).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The duplicate lookup reads by index
decisions.decision: A row's duplicate by content is looked up twice, each by index: as the transaction is now (budget, kind, amount, date) and as first imported (budget, original amount and date, imported transactions only); the earlier match wins. The values as first imported belong to imported transactions only (a check constraint).
decisions.why: The one-query form could not use an index and scanned the budget for every row: 6 to 7.5 s for a 500-row preview at 45 000 transactions (re-review M-3).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Token windows by whole minutes
decisions.decision: A token's calls and rows are kept by minute; the whole minute a call was made in counts, so a call counts toward the hour for at least 60 and at most 61 minutes, and toward the day for at least 24 hours and at most 24 hours and 1 minute. The limits hold over any 60 minutes and any 24 hours.
decisions.why: Counting minutes strictly after now minus an hour let a call drop out after 59 minutes (re-review should-fix 8); one row per minute keeps the bookkeeping bounded.
rejected: One row per call: unbounded rows for refused calls.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A token adds only to its own batches
decisions.decision: A token adds chunks only to a batch it created; any other existing batch id (a member's, another token's, another budget's) answers import_batch_conflict, also for a chunk already recorded, so a token cannot read another batch's answers.
decisions.why: A token knowing a member's batch id could add to it and replay its chunks (re-review should-fix 7).

decisions.title: The token call takes its arguments as text
decisions.decision: import_with_token takes the batch id, the chunk and the statement dates as text and checks them itself (invalid_batch, invalid_chunk, invalid_date), so a malformed argument answers its code instead of a raw cast error. What happens before the function runs cannot be caught by it: a body that is not JSON (PGRST102), or nested so deep that parsing exceeds the stack (54001), is answered by PostgREST or the database parser.
decisions.why: Raw 22P02 and 22008 errors with a datestyle hint reached anonymous callers (re-review should-fix 6).

decisions.title: "Import anyway" imports the row previewed
decisions.decision: A valid row that was skipped is kept as the preview showed it, its free text cleaned (description, merchant, bank transaction id, details), so importing it anyway imports that row and a later import of the same statement line finds it by its bank id. An invalid row is kept as before (bounded, D-378).
decisions.why: The kept row was the raw text cut to the limit before cleaning: a padded description or bank id was imported shorter than previewed and no longer matched (re-review should-fix 4).

decisions.title: A moved start never removes interest (answers Q-282)
decisions.decision: move_period_start, and any other change of a period's start, is refused with interest_before_opening while the new start would be on or before the opening of a debt that has an interest entry in that period; preview_move_period_start refuses the same way. Nothing is removed, so a start moved and moved back loses nothing, and debt_interest.balance always agrees with the history.
decisions.why: Removing the entry made a round trip lose the interest for good and left the next entry computed on a balance the history no longer shows (Q-282).
rejected: Suspending the entry and restoring it: the later entries disagree with the history while it is suspended.
Recomputing every later entry: amounts the member has seen change, and a move back still loses the entry.

decisions.title: The CSV decimal mark is read from the whole file, or asked
decisions.decision: Each amount cell says a point, a comma, either (no mark: -350, 1'234) or ambiguous (one mark followed by exactly three digits, a whole part of one to three digits: 1.200, 1,200). Both marks: the last one is the decimal mark; one mark twice groups thousands. Over every amount of the mapped columns: one reading settles it for every line (ambiguous lines follow it); only "either": a point, which changes no value and is not remembered; ambiguous and nothing settling it: the member must choose, and the screen says it could not be decided, naming the lines; a point on some lines and a comma on others: the file is refused, naming those lines, and no choice reads it. A choice made on the screen wins; a mapping remembered from an earlier file keeps its mark only if the member chose it or its file settled it (remembered mappings now carry version 2; older ones lose the assumed point). Under a settled point, 1.200 reads as 1.20 (trailing zeros of three decimals were already accepted, D-444).
decisions.why: Review M-1: -1.200 was read as CHF 1.20 because the mark defaulted to a point.
rejected: Refuse every three-digit fraction: a settled file would lose its readable lines.
Guess from the language of the header names: not reliable.

decisions.title: CSV bytes: encodings, control characters and a first line of data
decisions.decision: A CSV file is decoded on the device (csv-decode, a small module of the start screen): UTF-16 LE/BE by its byte-order mark or by NULs in every other byte, else UTF-8, else Windows-1252; a UTF-16 file that does not decode, or a text whose first 20 000 characters hold more than 2 % control characters, is refused with its reason before anything is read. A control character (C0 but tab and line ends, DEL, C1) is removed from each cell and its line named in a note. A first line holding a date and an amount is taken as a row: the header box opens unticked with a note saying why, and the date, amount and description columns are guessed from the content. A file with more rows than a batch takes (100 parts of 500, R-IMPORT-208) is refused on the mapping step, with the number and the advice to split it.
decisions.why: Review S-9, S-12, S-13.

decisions.title: The token secret is created outside the query library
decisions.decision: The token dialog calls create_import_token itself (its own pending and error state, then invalidates the token list), so no mutation exists whose options or closures could keep the secret; the secret is in the dialog's state only and set to null when it closes. rejected: A mutation with gcTime 0: the closure lives until the cache removes it, and the setter still reaches the state while the component is mounted.

decisions.title: Preview calls are limited, paused for the run, and a busy budget is not a refusal
decisions.decision: The preview of a part waits for a free place among two; a part asked again meanwhile drops its waiting call. Once the import starts, no part is previewed (the queries are disabled, so the invalidation after the run reads nothing again). A statement timeout (57014, HTTP 500) is "busy" (errors.busy): the preview asks again up to three times, one, two and three seconds apart, then says so with "Check again"; the run sends the same part again after the same waits, says "the budget was busy: part n was sent again", and after three stops with "Continue in a moment", which resends the same batch.
