decisions.title: Occurrences are keyed by date, not by period
decisions.decision: An occurrence of a planned transfer is identified by a date, its key, never by a period. A fixed-day transfer follows the calendar exactly like a subscription: a cadence (monthly, quarterly or yearly), a first date that sets the phase, and a nominal day clamped to the month's length, its dates computed by the subscriptions' own schedule code; each date is the key and the due date of an occurrence of the period that contains it, so a short period can have none and a long one two, and a yearly payment is one occurrence a year. A pay-date transfer has one occurrence per pay date of its income in the period: for a chosen income in force, each of its actual pay dates in the period (key = that date); otherwise (the primary income, a chosen income not in force or deleted) one occurrence keyed by the period's scheduled pay date. Every period stores the scheduled pay date of the salary that started it (periods.pay_key): the previous period's projected end plus one by the projection rule when the period is created, the first period's start for the first; a reopen deletes the merged period with its key, and recording that salary again creates the same key. A period is never without a key: when that date is already another period's, it takes the next scheduled pay date no period has (D-490); a key two periods give a transfer (switching between its chosen income and the primary one) belongs to the earlier period. Marks are stored by transfer and key.
decisions.why: The review (M2, M3): keyed by period, one real transfer could be recorded twice after a reopen, and short and long periods produced transactions the bank never made. A key that does not move with boundaries makes "the same occurrence" well defined across early and late salaries, reopens and boundary moves. A stored scheduled pay date is needed because the primary income's history is not versioned per period (a primary switch would otherwise change every past key).
rejected: Keying the primary income's occurrence by the period's start: a salary recorded again on another day would make a member's mark a different occurrence.
Computing the scheduled pay date from the current primary income's terms: a primary switch or a pay-day edit would move past keys and orphan marks.
Giving a colliding period the next scheduled date: every later period's key would shift by a month.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16
owner-request: database developer decision for the step 7 occurrence model, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A transfer's first counted day
decisions.decision: A transfer counts from the first day of the period it is created in, or corrected from, or that period's scheduled pay date when it is earlier (a salary that came late): transfers.starts_on. Nothing before it is planned, and a done date must lie on or after it (before_transfer_start). It stays a date when a reopen moves the transfer's first period into the reopened one, so that period's own earlier payday is not planned. Created with no period named and no first date after the period has started, it counts from the day it was created (D-493).
decisions.why: The handover's trap: a transfer created in a merged period had its first period moved into the reopened one, which then had its own occurrence of a payday the transfer never knew (the root of M2).
rejected: Freezing first_seq through a reopen: the registry merges validity for every record kind alike.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16
owner-request: database developer decision for the step 7 occurrence model, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Due dates of occurrences
decisions.decision: A fixed-day occurrence is due on its date, never capped. A pay-date occurrence is due on the actual pay date plus the offset (0 to 31 days), never after the last day of the period that contains the actual pay date; for the primary income the actual pay date is the period's start, whatever moved it. Answers Q-224: a fixed-day transfer has no occurrence in a period that does not contain its date.
decisions.why: What the bank does: a standing order runs on its calendar date whatever the salary does.
rejected: Capping a fixed date onto a short period's last day (two transfers a few days apart, one the bank never made).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The transfers' watermark is a date and moves back on every change of the plan
decisions.decision: Each transfer has a watermark by due date (settled_through: every occurrence due up to it is settled), the due date of its next automatic linked occurrence waiting (next_due) and a flag that its plan changed (needs_check). Triggers move the watermark back and set the flag on every change of what the plan derives from: a period inserted, a boundary moved or a period deleted, an income's terms or validity (for transfers choosing it), the transfer's terms or validity, and every removal of a mark. The catch-up then looks at the transfer again from its watermark (D-424). The writes that change the plan (transfer edits and ends, marks, income edits and removals, a primary switch, member removal, every boundary operation and reopen) run that catch-up before they answer, so their answer shows the result; any other path is settled by the next catch-up (my_budgets.caught_up is false until then). Never created twice: one mark per transfer and key, one transaction per mark; none skipped: the watermark passes a due date only once every occurrence due by then is settled.
decisions.why: M1 and the reviewer's dead ends came from a watermark by period that changes of the plan did not move consistently; triggers cover every path, including those of earlier steps.
rejected: A deferred trigger at commit: a test transaction (pgTAP) never commits, and the write's answer would be stale.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16
owner-request: database developer decision for the step 7 occurrence model, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: What the catch-up removes and what stays
decisions.decision: After a change of the plan the catch-up removes its own marks (and their transactions) whose occurrence is no longer planned or no longer due, and creates the transactions of the automatic linked occurrences due without a mark. It keeps its own mark of an occurrence still planned whatever the new terms: made manual, unlinked, another amount or category (what was recorded on the due date stays; undo leads out). A moved period start is the exception: the catch-up's own marks whose due date the move changed are made again on the new due date (D-491). Ending a transfer turns the catch-up's marks of occurrences it removes into kept marks (by_catch_up false), so nothing recorded goes. A member's mark never goes with a change of the plan: one whose occurrence is no longer planned is listed in the checklist of the period containing its date, flagged (planned false; is_ended when the transfer is not in force there), until undone or until its occurrence is planned again (the salary recorded again).
decisions.why: The brief's reconcile step, read together with its rule that an occurrence keeps its mark or transaction when the transfer is made manual, corrected or ended: only an occurrence that is gone or not yet due loses the catch-up's transaction.
rejected: Removing the catch-up's transaction when the transfer is made manual from the current period: the bank did the transfer on its due date.
Removing a member's mark whose occurrence is gone: it would go silently.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16
owner-request: database developer decision for the step 7 occurrence model, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Committed figures and the money flow use the monthly share
decisions.decision: A quarterly or yearly transfer counts its amount divided by its months, rounded half up to the rappen by the subscriptions' own rule (private.subscription_monthly_cost), in every committed figure and in the money flow, in each period it is in force; a monthly or pay-date transfer counts its amount. The reads carry the real amount and cadence beside it (transfer_overview: amount, cadence, monthly_amount; get_money_flow: amount is the monthly share, planned_amount and cadence the real ones). Answers Q-220 with D-420.
decisions.why: A yearly payment counted in full in one period and nothing in the others would make the plan of most periods wrong; subscriptions already count a monthly share.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A deleted income does not reset a transfer silently
decisions.decision: When an income a transfer's terms name is deleted outright (added and removed in the same period), the terms keep that they named one (transfer_versions.income_gone): the transfer follows the primary income and says so (follows_primary), like a chosen income that ended.
decisions.why: The review: the foreign key set the income to null and the transfer looked as if it had always followed the primary income.
rejected: Refusing to delete an income a transfer names: removing a mistaken income would need the transfer edited first.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A catch-up step creates a bounded number of transactions
decisions.decision: One catch-up step creates at most 4000 subscription charges and transfer transactions per budget and statement, and stops after about two seconds of work once it has created some (limit_catch_up_work); what is left stays due, none skipped, for the next step. A step that stops before creating every one due answers at least 1 from ensure_periods, so 0 still means caught up, and my_budgets.caught_up stays false.
decisions.why: The review measured 11 s for one ensure_periods call over HTTP once a full budget got room for 36 000 transactions, and a statement timeout at 48 000.
rejected: A lower transaction limit: the backlog would still be unbounded per step.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The previews run the write and roll it back
decisions.decision: preview_create_transfer, preview_update_transfer and preview_reopen run the write itself in a subtransaction they roll back, and compare the transfers' marks before and after: the catch-up's transactions created and removed, the members' marks whose occurrence is no longer planned or planned again. The create and edit previews give these as counts on every row (created_at_once_count, transactions_removed_count, marks_unplanned_count) and, when the terms govern no occurrence, one row with only the counts (occurrence_date null); preview_reopen gives one row per occurrence (transaction_removed, transaction_created, mark_unplanned, mark_planned_again). preview_end_transfer counts the occurrences it removes and the marks and transactions it keeps. A preview that runs the write takes the budget lock like the write.
decisions.why: Every preview of a change that the catch-up follows must say truthfully what it does; the write's own code is the only way to be sure.
rejected: Recomputing the effect with what-if boundaries: a second implementation of the plan.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16
owner-request: database developer decision for the step 7 occurrence model, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Marks name their occurrence
decisions.decision: mark_transfer_done, skip_transfer, mark_transfer_not_done and undo_transfer_mark keep p_period_id and take an optional p_occurrence_date, needed only when the period lists several occurrences of the transfer (occurrence_required); a date that is not one of them answers transfer_not_in_force. The checklist has one row per occurrence with its key. Undo puts any mark back to the unmarked state for the terms then in force (a manual occurrence to do; an automatic one assumed done, its transaction made within the call when linked and due); the catch-up's transaction of an automatic linked occurrence is that state already (nothing_to_undo: mark it not done). A mark listed but no longer planned can only be undone, which removes it with its transaction.
decisions.why: Several occurrences in a period (D-420), and no state from which no call leads out (the review's dead ends).
rejected: Marks keyed by period: a long period has two occurrences.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Reopen and the transfers (revised again)
decisions.decision: A reopen moves no mark: marks are keyed by date (D-420). The merged period's scheduled pay date is no longer planned, so the catch-up's transaction of a primary pay-date occurrence there goes, and comes back once the salary is recorded again (dated the day it came); a member's mark there stays, listed by its date and flagged, and is the same occurrence again once the salary is recorded again. Fixed-day occurrences keep their dates and their marks. A transfer created in the merged period counts from its first counted day (D-421), so the reopened period gets no occurrence of its own earlier payday. preview_reopen lists each effect per occurrence (D-428).
decisions.why: M2: a reopen followed by recording the salary again must leave exactly one transaction for that payday's standing order.
rejected: Moving the merged period's marks to the reopened period (D-382): the same payday then exists twice once the salary is recorded again.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 7 occurrence model redesign, after the independent review of 747686c, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: create_transfer's full signature is set up after the retry guard
decisions.decision: create_transfer takes p_cadence and p_first_date. Its retry guard (D-390) comes from the client-request migration, which runs after step 7's; that migration is not changed, so step 7 keeps the first signature for it to wrap, and the migration 20261122100000_transfer_schedule.sql replaces the guarded call with the full signature over step 7's private.create_transfer_core.
decisions.why: Every migration but step 7's is frozen; nothing is deployed, but the order of the files is fixed.
rejected: Editing the client-request migration.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for the step 7 occurrence model, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: How a preview runs the write
decisions.decision: A preview that runs the write (D-428: preview_create_transfer, preview_update_transfer, preview_reopen, preview_update_income, preview_set_primary_income, preview_move_period_start) takes the budget lock before it reads the revisions and marks it compares, so behind a member's write in flight it waits and then previews what that write left instead of answering record_changed; inside its subtransaction the catch-up step starts afresh (its bound of transactions and its time, D-427), as the write's own statement would. preview_update_transfer with an amount alone (no other term, no p_from_period_id) runs no write and takes no lock: it applies the write's checks of the new terms and answers the plan as it is at the new amount, every count 0.
decisions.why: A preview re-asked at keystroke pace must not fail because another member saved meanwhile, must hit a limit exactly where the write would, and should not queue behind writers for the most common edit (the amount), which moves no occurrence and touches no transaction already made.
rejected: Reading before taking the lock: behind a writer the write then refuses with record_changed after waiting.
Running the write for an amount alone too: it waits for every writer of the budget for an answer known without it.
source: owner-request: coordinator follow-up on the step 7 redesign (2264e82), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A budget behind with its charges or transfers is catching up
decisions.decision: catch_up_gate also answers catching_up (before the lock, doing nothing) when a subscription charge or an automatic transfer's transaction due more than 62 days before today (or the budget's end) is not made yet and the budget has room for transactions; a full budget is not behind (its charges and transactions wait for room, as before). Only ensure_periods and get_current_period then catch up, one bounded step at a time.
decisions.why: With all its periods there but tens of thousands of transfer transactions still to make (a budget opened after decades), every read and write passed the gate and queued on the budget lock behind the others' steps (each up to two seconds), so a screen of eight calls at once ran into the statement timeout (18 timeouts in 40 rounds at 40 years).
rejected: Making the step smaller: the queue grows with the number of calls a screen makes, not with the step.
source: owner-request: coordinator follow-up on the step 7 redesign (2264e82), 2026-11-16

decisions.title: A period is never without a key; occurrences are found by their key
decisions.decision: Every period has a scheduled pay date as its key (periods.pay_key). When the date the projection gives (the previous period's projected end plus one) is already another period's key (a salary recorded 15 or more days early, then the next one; several salaries in one month), the period takes the next scheduled pay date of the primary income's terms no period has. The key depends only on the earlier periods, so a reopen and the salary recorded again give the same key, and the backfill of existing budgets follows the same rule in order. Because a key can then lie a month or more from its period, every lookup of an occurrence goes by the stored key: the periods that can plan a key are the one whose pay_key it is and the one containing the date, wherever they lie (private.transfer_plan_keys). This covers transfer_planned, the checklist's marks planned elsewhere, the catch-up's check of its own marks, the previews' snapshot of marks, deleting a transaction (not done, not deleted) and end_transfer (a mark still planned is not frozen). When both periods give a transfer the same key, it belongs to the earlier one. Answers Q-260.
decisions.why: With the earlier rule a real payday lost its pay-date transfer after a salary that came 15 or more days early (one transfer for three salaries recorded in one month), and lookups that searched only the neighbouring periods missed keys two periods away: a mark listed twice, deleting its transaction deleted the mark so the catch-up created the transaction again, and ending a transfer froze a mark still planned.
rejected: Keying such a period by its actual start: a key is then not stable across a reopen and the salary recorded on another day.
Searching more neighbouring periods: any fixed window can be exceeded by repeated early salaries.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), M1 with C1, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Moving a period's start moves what the app recorded by itself
decisions.decision: After move_period_start, an automatic transaction the catch-up made for an occurrence of the two periods whose boundary moved sits on the occurrence's new due date, in the right period, exactly as after a reopen and the salary recorded on that day: the catch-up's own mark (by_catch_up) whose done date is not the new due date goes with its transaction and the catch-up makes it again (on the new due date, at the terms in force there; when that date is still ahead, once it is due). A member's own mark (done or skipped by hand, with its date) stays where the member put it. preview_move_period_start counts each moved transaction once removed and once created. The move's refusal for a debt's interest (interest_before_opening, D-467) is answered by the preview as by the write, with every count 0.
decisions.why: The member says when the salary really came; the standing order the app recorded on the old day then showed two transfers in the period before and none in the moved one, with a checklist row done before the period started, while saying the same thing another way (reopen, then record the salary) dated it on the new day.
rejected: Keeping the transaction on its old date (D-424 as first written): the two ways to say when the salary came gave different budgets.
Re-dating the transaction in place: a move would then keep an amount the terms no longer give, unlike a reopen and the salary recorded again.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), M3, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Ending a chosen income never rewrites what is already recorded
decisions.decision: When the income a pay-date transfer chose ends from the current period (remove_income, remove_member, leave_budget), the day it ended is kept (incomes.ended_on). In that period the transfer keeps the income's occurrences due on or before that day, with their marks and transactions, and has the primary's occurrence only if it was not due yet that day; from the next period it follows the primary income. Ended from an earlier period (a correction) or deleted outright (D-426), the transfer follows the primary income in those periods as before.
decisions.why: Ending the income after its transfer was made removed that transaction and recorded one dated weeks earlier for the primary salary, with no preview for these calls.
rejected: A preview for remove_income, remove_member and leave_budget: with nothing rewritten there is nothing for it to announce about the transfers.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), S2, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: Creating a transfer records nothing dated before today unless the member asks
decisions.decision: create_transfer with neither p_from_period_id nor p_first_date plans nothing before today: a fixed day's first date is the first date with that day on or after today, and a pay-date transfer counts from today (starts_on), so a payday of the current period already past has no occurrence. Naming a period (the current one included) or giving a first date asks for the earlier occurrences: they are planned, the automatic linked ones already due are created at once, and preview_create_transfer counts them (created_at_once).
decisions.why: A fixed-day transfer created on 20 November for the 5th recorded a transaction dated 5 November that never happened.
rejected: Asking in the form only: the database would still record the past by default for any other client.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), C3, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The dashboard's transfer counts are a read of their own
decisions.decision: transfers_to_do and transfers_overdue are no longer columns of my_budgets: get_transfers_to_do(p_budget_id) answers them for a member (one row; no catch-up). my_budgets, read on every page and after every write, no longer computes two periods' plan for every budget the user belongs to. No screen read them yet.
decisions.why: At the documented limits my_budgets took about 100 ms, 82 of them the transfer counts, also when they were not selected (the screens select every column).
rejected: Keeping the columns and making the plan cheaper: the plan of two periods for every budget a user belongs to stays the dominant cost of a read made on every page.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the independent review of the step 7 redesign (2264e82), S6, 2026-11-16

conventions.statement: Money is integer rappen in code.
Money is integer rappen in the database.
Money is formatted only at the edge.
Every table has row-level security enabled.
A table's row-level security is enabled, with policies, in the same migration that creates it.
Access rules use the shared membership helpers in the `private` schema; a new table's policies call them rather than re-deriving membership.
Period, pay-date and versioning logic has one implementation, in the database (SQL functions).
Period, pay-date and versioning logic is tested with pgTAP.
The client reads period, pay-date and versioning results; it never recomputes them.
Client queries for budget data are keyed by budget id.
Database tests (pgTAP, `supabase/tests/`) must pass on a database that already holds data: scope assertions to the test's own rows.
Every table gets tests proving what another user cannot do.
Every table gets tests proving what an anonymous visitor cannot do.
Calendar dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and timestamps are different things.
Never run a calendar date through a time zone.
The production Content-Security-Policy is `script-src 'self'`.
No inline scripts.
Every user-facing string exists in both `en` and `fr`.
Never commit secrets.
Only the Supabase URL and publishable (anon) key reach the browser, through `VITE_` variables.
A change in behaviour or a new decision updates `spec/spec.json` in the same change.
Generated files (`docs/spec.md` and the generated block of `CLAUDE.md`) are never edited by hand: change `spec/spec.json` and run `npm run spec:render`.
Every active rule or convention with enforcement `test` has a test whose description names its id, and no test names an id that is unknown or not active.
Ids are stable: never renumber or reuse one; retire a rule or supersede a decision instead of deleting it.
conventions.rationale: spec:check only notices an id that disappeared since the base commit (HEAD by default); it cannot tell a reused id from the original.

openQuestions.question: May a member add, edit or remove an income that belongs to another member?
openQuestions.context: The source says "Each member adds their own incomes (person A adds income A, person B adds income B)" and also "every member can read and edit everything in the budget". The step 2 code lets any member add an income for another member (add_income p_user_id) and change any income's terms.

openQuestions.question: How is one twelfth of a yearly amount rounded to whole rappen, and must twelve monthly shares add up to the yearly amount exactly?
openQuestions.context: Yearly amounts are stored as yearly and shown as one twelfth per month; amounts are integer rappen, so most yearly amounts do not divide by twelve.

openQuestions.question: Which "budget total" does the amount left to assign use: the monthly total of the incomes in force now, or the income total of a given period?
openQuestions.context: The source defines the amount left to assign as "budget total minus the sum of expectations" and the budget as starting "from the monthly total of its incomes"; incomes are versioned per period.

openQuestions.question: What does the sign of a transaction amount mean (spending, refund, extra income), and may a transaction be put on a category that has subcategories?
openQuestions.context: A transaction "has an amount, a date, and a category or subcategory"; nothing says how refunds or money coming in are recorded, nor whether a parent category with subcategories can hold transactions directly.

openQuestions.question: Can a transaction be linked to both a debt and a subscription, or to at most one of them?
openQuestions.context: The source says "optional link to a debt or a subscription".

openQuestions.question: Which cadences does a subscription support, what is its "pay date" (a date or a day of the month), and does the weekend rule apply to it?
openQuestions.context: A subscription "has a price, a pay date, a cadence, and a category"; nothing more is said.

openQuestions.question: How does the interest rate affect a debt's remaining amount and expected end date, and is the remaining amount the principal minus the transactions assigned to it?
openQuestions.context: A debt has "a principal, an optional interest rate, and a planned monthly payment"; "a transaction assigned to a debt reduces the remaining amount".

openQuestions.question: Which payday does a planned transfer refer to ("payday + 2 days"): the actual pay date of the primary income (period start), or of a chosen income?
openQuestions.context: Example from the source: "payday + 2 days: 1000 CHF from A to Savings". A budget can have several incomes with different pay days.
source: domain: Account and planned transfer (money flow)

openQuestions.question: What makes an imported row a duplicate (same date, amount and description; an import id; something else)?
openQuestions.context: The import function "skips duplicates"; nothing defines a duplicate.
source: domain: Import (including by a Claude session)

openQuestions.question: Is browsing past periods part of step 3 (period progress view) or step 5 (period comparison charts)?
openQuestions.context: The source lists "Users can browse past periods and compare them (for example a yearly chart)" in one sentence; the build order names a "period progress view" in step 3 and "period comparison charts" in step 5. This spec puts both under step 5 for now.

openQuestions.question: What exactly stays editable in a past period: its transactions only, or also its boundaries and other data?
openQuestions.context: "Past periods stay editable" comes right after back-dated transactions, while versioning says edits to incomes, expectations, subscriptions and debts never rewrite the past. The step 2 code already lets members move the boundaries of past periods.
source: domain: Versioning: edits never rewrite the past

openQuestions.question: What is a period's surplus or deficit measured against: its income total, or the sum of its expectations?
openQuestions.context: "At the end of a period, category balances reset. The period's surplus or deficit is shown as its result."

openQuestions.question: How does the import script a Claude session runs authenticate, given that Claude does not get raw database access to real data?
openQuestions.context: The import is reachable "from a script in this repo that a Claude Code session can run", and "Claude does not get raw database access to real data". The likely reading is that it calls the import function as a signed-in member, but the source does not say.
source: domain: Import (including by a Claude session)

openQuestions.question: How are merchant-to-category rules created: automatically when a user categorises an imported transaction, or explicitly by the user?
openQuestions.context: "Merchant-to-category rules are saved so categorisation improves over time."
source: domain: Import (including by a Claude session)

openQuestions.question: Are planned transfers versioned like incomes (edits effective from the current period)?
openQuestions.context: The versioning rule lists incomes, category expectations, subscriptions and debts; it does not mention accounts or planned transfers, which also appear on a per-period checklist.
source: domain: Versioning: edits never rewrite the past
domain: Account and planned transfer (money flow)

openQuestions.question: Should the database return "today" (or the day number within the current period) so that the client never uses the browser's date?
openQuestions.context: The dashboard shows "day N of M" of the current period; the contract returns the period but not the Europe/Zurich date the database decided it with, so N comes from the browser (D-048) and can differ around midnight or in another time zone.

openQuestions.question: Should create_budget take the end date, so that a budget with an end date is created in one atomic step?
openQuestions.context: The first-run form asks for an optional end date; create_budget has no such argument, so the client calls set_budget_end_date afterwards. If that second call fails, the budget exists without its end date and the user is told so.

openQuestions.question: What should happen to a budget and its incomes when a member's or the owner's account is deleted?
openQuestions.context: No client path deletes accounts yet. Today, deleting the owner's account deletes their budgets for every member (R-BUDGET-016), and deleting a member's account keeps their incomes with a null owner without the member rules: an income that is primary stays active and primary (review finding 8). Settle before any account-deletion feature.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

openQuestions.question: When two members edit the same income at the same time, should the second save be refused (for example with a version check) instead of silently overwriting the first?
openQuestions.context: Today the last write wins without a warning: update_income_terms and the rename both replace what is there. Every member can edit every income (D-045), so two members of a household can edit the same salary from two browsers.

openQuestions.question: How is a half rappen rounded when one twelfth (or another monthly share) falls exactly between two rappen, and do the totals (left to assign, results, committed amounts) add up the rounded monthly shares or round the exact sum?
openQuestions.context: D-100 says one twelfth rounded to the nearest rappen. A yearly amount that is 6 rappen more than a multiple of 12 gives exactly half a rappen (CHF 1.50 a year gives 12.5 rappen), and the tie rule is not given. D-110 also needs a monthly cost for quarterly, half-yearly and yearly subscriptions; the answers do not say it uses the same rounding.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: What happens to the transactions already on a category when the user adds its first subcategory?
openQuestions.context: D-102: when a category has subcategories, a transaction goes on a subcategory, never on the parent. A category without subcategories holds transactions directly, so adding a subcategory later would leave them on the parent (they could be moved, refused, or kept for past periods only).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: How is money coming in that is neither a salary nor a refund (a gift, a resale, a reimbursement from a third party) recorded?
openQuestions.context: Q-004 asked about extra income; D-102 answers spending and refunds only. Incomes are monthly, and one-off incomes are deferred (D-038).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Can a transaction be added to, or moved into, a category that has ended, when its date falls in a period where the category was still in force?
openQuestions.context: D-105 lets transactions in past periods be added and edited freely; D-107 ends a deleted category from the current period while past periods keep it.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: When are automatic subscription charges created, given that there is no server: are charge dates missed while nobody opened the app created later, back-dated, and is a charge whose transaction was deleted or answered "did not go through" ever created again?
openQuestions.context: D-109: the transaction is created on the charge date, can be deleted, and is removed when the user says it did not go through. The app is a static SPA on Supabase (D-003), so creation can only happen when the database is next called. Also open: whether editing the subscription (a new version) changes charges already created.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: When in a period is a debt's interest applied (at its start or end, before or after that period's payments), how is it rounded to the rappen, and does a payment exactly equal to the interest count as "never ends"?
openQuestions.context: D-113: once per period, one twelfth of the yearly rate is applied to the remaining balance and added to it; when the planned payment does not cover the interest the app says the debt never ends. Periods run salary to salary, not by calendar month (D-080), and the expected end date needs a date for each future interest step.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Are identical rows within the same file duplicates of each other, are refunds and manually entered transactions compared too, and is "import anyway" chosen per row or for all skipped rows?
openQuestions.context: D-115 compares an imported row with existing transactions. Two identical purchases on one day (two coffees) appear as two identical rows in one export; the answer does not say whether the second is skipped.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: What identifies a merchant for a merchant-to-category rule: the whole description, a part of it, or a field of the bank export?
openQuestions.context: D-117 offers "always put this merchant in this category?". Bank descriptions often carry a date, a card number or a location around the merchant name, so an exact match on the description would rarely match again. The sample statements show that the bank cuts merchant names at 24 characters, that one merchant can be printed in different capitals or with different processor prefixes, and that chains add a branch number (docs/import-sources.md). The card bill adds a merchant category line.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Which product is "One", what export formats do Migros Bank, Raiffeisen, One, Yuh and Twint actually offer, and can the product owner provide sample export files?
openQuestions.context: D-119 asks for presets for these five sources. "One" may be Viseca's "one" credit-card portal; that is unconfirmed. Twint may offer no export at all. Sample export files are needed before the presets can be built.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: For a planned transfer on a fixed day of the month, is the day clamped to the month's length and does a weekend rule apply; may a pay-date offset be negative; and what happens to a transfer whose chosen income ends?
openQuestions.context: D-120 allows an offset in days from a chosen income's actual pay date, or a fixed day of the month. Subscriptions clamp and use no weekend rule (D-108), but nothing says the same for transfers. An income ends when it is removed or its member leaves (R-MEMBER-007).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: On which date is the transaction of an automatic transfer linked to a category created, does it wait for confirmation like a subscription charge, and does unmarking a manual transfer as done remove its transaction?
openQuestions.context: D-122: when a transfer linked to a category is marked done, or when it is automatic, its transaction is created in that category. Automatic transfers are assumed done (R-ACCOUNT-004); subscription charges, also automatic, wait for confirmation (D-109).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should an edit be able to apply from the next period ("from the next salary") instead of the current one?
openQuestions.context: An edit always applies to the current period (R-VERSION-001), so a raise entered before its salary arrives changes the current period's total. A later option could key the edit to the next period, which needs a way to hold a change for a period that does not exist yet without breaking "nothing keyed beyond the latest period" (R-VERSION-011).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should a category's expectation be scaled for a period much longer or shorter than a month, such as a reopened period of 60 to 92 days?
openQuestions.context: Each expectation counts once per period, like an income (D-147, R-INCOME-011). A reopened period (R-PERIOD-023) can last up to 92 days and still expects one month of each category, while two months of spending land in it.

openQuestions.question: Should a category whose subcategories have all been deleted become an ordinary category again, able to hold an expectation and transactions?
openQuestions.context: D-141: a category stays a group once it had a subcategory, so an empty group expects nothing and takes no transaction until a subcategory is added.

openQuestions.question: Should an ended category be restorable (in force again from the current period) instead of being created anew?
openQuestions.context: Ending is final today (R-CATEGORY-072); a new category with the same name starts a new history, so past periods and the new one show two separate rows.

openQuestions.question: Are future-dated transactions needed (a bill known in advance), and if so how should they behave when the period they fall in has not started yet?
openQuestions.context: D-145 limits dates to today. Planned recurring charges are subscriptions (step 4), whose charges are created on the charge date (D-109).
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should two members reordering the same categories at the same time be detected, like other concurrent edits?
openQuestions.context: A reorder is refused when the set of categories changed meanwhile (R-CATEGORY-096), but two reorders of the same set: the later wins. Ordering is not a revision of a category (D-142), so a reorder never blocks another member's edit.

openQuestions.question: Will any member import statements in German, Italian or English, and can the product owner provide a sample of each?
openQuestions.context: D-134 supports the French versions first. The labels, and possibly the date and number formats, differ in other languages; each language needs a sample before its parser can be tested.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Do Migros Bank e-banking and Yuh also offer a CSV or camt.053 export of the same transactions, and should the import prefer it to the PDF?
openQuestions.context: A structured export would be sturdier than reading a PDF layout, which the banks can change without notice. The samples provided are PDF only.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: How is a transfer to another member of the household treated, for example a standing order to a partner at the same address: an expense, a transfer between the household's accounts, or something else?
openQuestions.context: The Migros Bank statement shows no IBAN for a payee, so the import recognises an own transfer only by the holder's name and address (D-129). A standing order to another person at the same address looks like any other payment.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: What exactly is remembered when the user imports or skips a flagged entry: the choice per kind of entry, per counterparty or per account, and for the whole budget or for the member only?
openQuestions.context: D-129 says the choice is remembered and proposed next time, without saying for what.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: When does a salary credit match one of the budget's incomes: same amount, same payer, a date near the expected pay date, or a combination; and what happens when the amount differs from the planned income?
openQuestions.context: D-130 skips a salary credit that matches an income. The Migros Bank statement marks it "Paiement de salaire" with the employer's name, but gives no reference to the income.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: When a credit is reviewed as a refund, in which period and category does it count, and can it reduce a category below zero?
openQuestions.context: D-130 proposes other credits as a refund in a category or as extra income. TWINT money received from a person is often a share of a bill paid earlier, possibly in another period.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should regular investment purchases (a savings plan) count as spending in the period, or as savings that the money flow of step 7 shows as a transfer?
openQuestions.context: D-131 imports them as ordinary transactions until accounts exist. On the Yuh statement a purchase is a debit like any other, with the security, quantity, price and fees on its continuation lines.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: How is an imported card or bank line reconciled with a transaction already in the budget for the same charge, such as an automatic subscription charge or a manually entered expense?
openQuestions.context: R-IMPORT-070 treats a row as a duplicate only when date, amount and description are the same; a statement line has the bank's description and often a different date (D-128), so the same charge would be counted twice.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Are cash withdrawals expenses when they are made, or transfers to a cash wallet whose spending is entered by hand?
openQuestions.context: No cash withdrawal appeared in the samples, but the Migros Bank account statement will show them.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Does the household have other cards or accounts to import, such as a partner's card, a supplementary card on the same card account, or another member's Yuh account, and should each import be tied to one of the budget's accounts?
openQuestions.context: The samples cover one debit card, one credit card and one Yuh account of one member. A card bill has one section per card. Step 7 introduces accounts.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should a past boundary moved by hand and then moved back to where the projection put it stop being marked "set by hand"?
openQuestions.context: move_period_start and record_early_pay_date always set periods.end_is_manual = true, also when the date goes back to its original day, and the contract has no way to clear the mark on a past period (set_expected_pay_date resets only the current period's end). The client cannot tell a past boundary that matches the schedule (C-LOGIC-003). The periods page now explains on the badge that the mark stays after moving back. Options: the database clears end_is_manual when a boundary is moved back to its projected date, or the mark is dropped for past periods.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should add_transaction take a client-generated id, so that a double-submitted or retried save records the transaction once?
openQuestions.context: The boundary operations name the period they act on (D-151), so a retry is refused; an add has no record to name yet. The review recorded a double-submitted add_transaction as two rows. The screens disable the button while saving, but a retry after a lost response would still record twice.

openQuestions.question: Should the database say where the schedule would put a period's start, and whether moving it back there would be accepted?
openQuestions.context: "Move this period's start back to the schedule" calls move_period_start without a date; the client cannot know the schedule's day (C-LOGIC-003), so the confirmation names no date and the action is offered even when the database will refuse it (invalid_boundary), which the dialog then says. Options: a period_summaries.scheduled_start column (null when it equals the start), or preview_move_period_start(p_period_id) returning the scheduled date and whether it fits between the neighbouring periods, so the action is offered only when it can work and names its date.

openQuestions.question: When the transaction limit holds automatic charges back, should the app tell the members?
openQuestions.context: D-176: charges wait, none skipped, until there is room; nothing tells the user that some are waiting. Reaching 50 000 transactions takes decades of normal use.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should a price change also update the charges already created and still awaiting confirmation?
openQuestions.context: D-170: charges already created never change; a member edits a charge awaiting confirmation like any transaction. A price rise announced after a charge was created leaves that charge at the old price.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should an old charge awaiting confirmation be confirmed automatically after some time?
openQuestions.context: D-175: a charge awaits confirmation until a member answers; the dashboard list can grow if nobody does. It counts in totals meanwhile (R-SUBSCRIPTION-078).
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the database give the total remaining across a budget's debts?
openQuestions.context: D-191: the debts page adds up debt_overview.remaining for the debts in force. A database total would follow C-LOGIC-003 to the letter and could exclude or include ended debts by rule.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should one call change a transaction and its debt link together?
openQuestions.context: D-194: changing the debt a transaction pays takes up to three calls (unlink, update, link), not atomic; a failure part-way leaves part of the change.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the transaction form also link a transaction to a subscription (a charge recorded by hand)?
openQuestions.context: add_transaction and link_transaction accept p_subscription_id; the step 4 screens offer only the debt link, as the brief asked. A charge recorded by hand would show as a subscription charge without being an automatic one.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the database give the terms a record had in force in a given period?
openQuestions.context: D-210: the correction forms read the version tables and pick the row in force themselves. A function per record (or one column on the views by period) would keep that rule in the database (C-LOGIC-001).
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 1, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the database say beforehand whether a removal from a given earlier period deletes?
openQuestions.context: D-214: removal_deletes describes a removal from now only; for an earlier period the dialogs say both outcomes.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 1, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Can an ended debt be restored, or a payment recorded after it ended?
openQuestions.context: D-209 freezes an ended debt: a payment forgotten before it was removed cannot be added any more. Undoing the removal is possible only as a correction of its end (none exists for debts yet).
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the app show progress while a very long absence is caught up?
openQuestions.context: D-201: after more than ten years away, reading a budget takes several ensure_periods calls (120 periods each); my_budgets.caught_up is false meanwhile and get_current_period answers no row.
source: owner-request: coordinator review of the step 4 database, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should transaction_list say that a payment's debt has ended?
openQuestions.context: D-209: a payment of an ended debt cannot be changed or deleted. transaction_list gives debt_id and debt_name only, so the transactions list reads debt_overview to know which payments are frozen and disable their actions. A column debt_ended (or a frozen flag) would let the list say so from its own row.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 2, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should get_debt_history also page newest first?
openQuestions.context: D-232: the history table shows the oldest events first because get_debt_history pages only in that order; for a long history the latest events, the ones a member usually looks for, are many pages away. A p_newest_first flag with the mirrored cursor would let the table start with them.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 4 screens review round 2, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should a category's average spent count only the periods where it was in force?
openQuestions.context: D-261: it divides by every completed period of the range, so a category added three periods ago averages over all twelve and looks smaller than its usual spending. Counting only periods in force would make the per-category averages not add up to the trend's average spent.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 5, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the current, still running period be compared by default, or the last completed one?
openQuestions.context: R-COMPARE-071 (coordinator decision): B defaults to the current period and A to the one before, so early in a period B shows little spending against a whole period A.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 5, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the number of budgets a user can belong to be limited?
openQuestions.context: D-264: my_budgets returns one row per budget the user belongs to. A user owns at most 20, but nothing limits the budgets they are invited to; past 1000 the API would cut the list. No screen pages it.
source: owner-request: coordinator finding on the step 5 database (API row limit), 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should the "to categorise" category count towards the 200 categories in force?
openQuestions.context: D-312: it is created even at the limit, then counts like any category, so a budget at 200 must end one before adding its own next category.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 6, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: When a period start moves onto or before a debt's opening and back again, how should the debt's interest come back, and should the later entries follow the history?
openQuestions.context: D-386 removes the period's interest entry when its start moves to on or before the opening (a trigger in the step 4 migration, private.drop_interest_before_opening) and adds nothing when it moves later again, because interest is computed once, when the period is created. So after a start moves onto the opening day and back, the debt is lower for good by the removed entry (120.00 in the re-review), and the next period's entry keeps the balance it was computed on (debt_interest.balance 1 212 000 while the history's balance before it is now 1 200 000). Options: (a) refuse the move while the period holds an interest entry of a debt opened on or after the new start (a refusal code, shown by preview_move_period_start as it already counts interest_removed): the history stays exact and nothing is lost, at the cost of a restriction; (b) keep the entry but mark it suspended while the start is on or before the opening, and restore it when the start moves after the opening again: the round trip is exact, but while suspended the later entries' balance disagrees by the suspended amount; (c) on any removal, recompute every later entry of that debt from the history: balance always agrees, but amounts the member has seen change, and a move back still loses the entry unless combined with (b). Recommended: (a). Any option changes the step 4 migration's trigger and its preview, which under D-450 is a new migration (or the money-flow rewrite), so it was not fixed in this round.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 6 database fix round 2 (re-review at 747686c), 2026-11-16
